VERIFY on the // bench: wheels off the ground, send +0.2 N·m to each, both must turn so the robot would roll forward. constexpr int DIR_LEFT = +1; constexpr int DIR_RIGHT = -1; constexpr float KT = 0.14f; // N·m/A (15T winding) constexpr float IQ_FULL_A = 16.5f; // iq command 2048 = 16.5 A constexpr int IQ_MAX_CMD = 2048; constexpr float ENC_COUNTS = 65536.f; // starting guess only: the firmware detects 14/15/16-bit at run time (boot log says which) constexpr uint32_t CAN_TIMEOUT_MS = 20; // no reply for this long -> motors off, FAULT // ---------------- IMU (MPU6050 / GY-521) ---------------- constexpr uint8_t MPU_ADDR = 0x68; // Map the sensor axes to the robot frame (X forward, Y left, Z up). Default: chip X forward, Y left, Z up. // VERIFY at rest, upright: the boot log must print acc ≈ (0, 0, +9.8); tilt forward -> ax becomes negative... see README. #define IMU_MAP_AX(a) ( (a)[0]) #define IMU_MAP_AY(a) ( (a)[1]) #define IMU_MAP_AZ(a) ( (a)[2]) #define IMU_MAP_GX(g) ( (g)[0]) #define IMU_MAP_GY(g) ( (g)[1]) #define IMU_MAP_GZ(g) ( (g)[2]) // ---------------- timing ---------------- constexpr uint32_t CONTROL_PERIOD_US = 2000; // 500 Hz: must match Params::DT in gains.hpp constexpr uint32_t TELEM_PERIOD_MS = 20; // 50 Hz to the Pi constexpr uint32_t CMD_TIMEOUT_MS = 300; // no command from the Pi -> stop driving (keep balancing) constexpr uint32_t PI_BAUD = 921600;

// ESP32 <-> Raspberry Pi UART protocol (921600 8N1). Mirrored in pi/robot/link.py: keep both in sync. // Frame: 0xA5 0x5A | type u8 | len u8 | payload[len] | crc8 (poly 0x07 over type, len, payload) // All multi-byte fields little-endian, floats IEEE-754 single. #pragma once #include <stdint.h> namespace pilink { constexpr uint8_t SYNC0 = 0xA5, SYNC1 = 0x5A; enum : uint8_t { MSG_CMD = 0x01, // Pi -> ESP32, >= 10 Hz while driving MSG_TELEM = 0x81, // ESP32 -> Pi, 50 Hz MSG_EVENT = 0x82, // ESP32 -> Pi, text line (boot info, faults) }; enum : uint8_t { // CmdMsg.flags F_ARM = 1 << 0, // request armed (edge-triggered on the ESP32: 0->1 arms) F_DISARM = 1 << 1, // request disarm (wins over F_ARM) F_AUTO_STANDUP = 1 << 2, // stand up by itself when lying F_OBST_STOP = 1 << 3, // sonar may block forward driving }; #pragma pack(push, 1) struct CmdMsg { // 16 bytes uint8_t mode; // 0 velocity, 1 turn-to (absolute heading), 2 turn-by (relative, new seq), 3 backflip (new seq), // 4 dock (velocity + lean back onto the dock on contact / new seq), 5 undock (new seq) uint8_t flags; uint16_t seq; float v; // m/s float yaw_rate; // rad/s float angle; // rad }; struct TelemMsg { // 57 bytes uint32_t t_ms; uint8_t state; // bot::State int8_t side; // +1 face-down, -1 back-down uint8_t flags; // bit0 armed, bit1 charging, bit2 sonar limiting, bit3 battery low, bit4 motor fault uint8_t tries; float pitch, roll, yaw; // rad float x, y, v; // m, m, m/s (odometry) float vbat; // V float sonar; // m, <0 none float tl, tr; // N·m float standup_adj; // learned stand-up energy correction float motor_temp; // °C, max of both uint8_t ir; // IR beacon, last 100 ms: bit 2i = receiver i heard 'all round', 2i+1 = 'centre'; // i: 0 front-left, 1 front-right, 2 back-left, 3 back-right }; #pragma pack(pop) static_assert(sizeof(CmdMsg) == 16, "CmdMsg layout"); static_assert(sizeof(TelemMsg) == 57, "TelemMsg layout"); inline uint8_t crc8(const uint8_t* d, int n, uint8_t crc = 0) { for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) { crc ^= d[i]; for (int b = 0; b < 8; ++b) crc = (crc & 0x80) ? (uint8_t)((crc << 1) ^ 0x07) : (uint8_t)(crc << 1); } return crc; } } // namespace pilink

// MPU6050 (GY-521) at 1 kHz internal rate, ±2000 dps (stand-up spins at up to ~20 rad/s), ±8 g. #pragma once #include <Arduino.h> #include <Wire.h> #include "config.h" struct ImuSample { float ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz; bool ok; }; #include "sim_hil.h" class Imu { public: #if defined(SIM_HIL) || defined(BENCH_CAN) bool begin() { simhil::begin(); return true; } ImuSample read() { // IMU sample from the physics host (already in m/s2, rad/s, chip axes) ImuSample s{}; float v[6]; s.ok = simhil::step(micros(), v); const float a[3] = {v[0], v[1], v[2]}, g[3] = {v[3], v[4], v[5]}; s.ax = IMU_MAP_AX(a); s.ay = IMU_MAP_AY(a); s.az = IMU_MAP_AZ(a); s.gx = IMU_MAP_GX(g); s.gy = IMU_MAP_GY(g); s.gz = IMU_MAP_GZ(g); return s; } #else bool begin() { Wire.begin(PIN_I2C_SDA, PIN_I2C_SCL, 400000); if (!wr(0x6B, 0x80)) return false; // reset delay(100); wr(0x6B, 0x01); // clock = gyro X PLL wr(0x1A, 0x02); // DLPF 94 Hz accel / 98 Hz gyro, 1 kHz wr(0x19, 0x00); // sample rate divider 0 -> 1 kHz wr(0x1B, 0x18); // gyro ±2000 dps wr(0x1C, 0x10); // accel ±8 g return rd8(0x75) == 0x68 || rd8(0x75) == 0x70 || rd8(0x75) == 0x98; // WHO_AM_I of MPU6050 clones } ImuSample read() { ImuSample s{}; uint8_t b[14]; Wire.beginTransmission(MPU_ADDR); Wire.write(0x3B); if (Wire.endTransmission(false) != 0 || Wire.requestFrom((int)MPU_ADDR, 14) != 14) { s.ok = false; return s; } for (int i = 0; i < 14; ++i) b[i] = Wire.read(); auto w = [&](int i) { return (int16_t)((b[i] << 8) | b[i + 1]); }; const float A = 9.80665f / 4096.f, G = (2000.f / 32768.f) * (PI / 180.f); const float a[3] = {w(0) * A, w(2) * A, w(4) * A}; const float g[3] = {w(8) * G, w(10) * G, w(12) * G}; s.ax = IMU_MAP_AX(a); s.ay = IMU_MAP_AY(a); s.az = IMU_MAP_AZ(a); s.gx = IMU_MAP_GX(g); s.gy = IMU_MAP_GY(g); s.gz = IMU_MAP_GZ(g); s.ok = true; return s; } private: bool wr(uint8_t r, uint8_t v) { Wire.beginTransmission(MPU_ADDR); Wire.write(r); Wire.write(v); return Wire.endTransmission() == 0; } uint8_t rd8(uint8_t r) { Wire.beginTransmission(MPU_ADDR); Wire.write(r); Wire.endTransmission(false); Wire.requestFrom((int)MPU_ADDR, 1); return Wire.read(); } #endif };

#include "ir_beacon.h" IrBeacon* IrBeacon::self_ = nullptr; const int IrBeacon::PINS[4] = {PIN_IR_FL, PIN_IR_FR, PIN_IR_BL, PIN_IR_BR}; void IRAM_ATTR IrBeacon::on(int i) { const uint32_t t = micros(); const bool hi = digitalRead(PINS[i]); portENTER_CRITICAL_ISR(&self_->mux_); self_->rx_[i].edge(hi, t); portEXIT_CRITICAL_ISR(&self_->mux_); } void IRAM_ATTR IrBeacon::isr0() { on(0); } void IRAM_ATTR IrBeacon::isr1() { on(1); } void IRAM_ATTR IrBeacon::isr2() { on(2); } void IRAM_ATTR IrBeacon::isr3() { on(3); }

// 4 x TSOP38238 on GPIO13..16 (front-left, front-right, back-left, back-right): pin-change interrupts time the // low pulses, ir_decode.h classifies them. bits() = what each receiver heard in the last 100 ms window. #pragma once #include <Arduino.h> #include "config.h" #include "ir_decode.h" class IrBeacon { public: void begin() { self_ = this; for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) pinMode(PINS[i], INPUT); // TSOP has its own pull-up attachInterrupt(digitalPinToInterrupt(PINS[0]), isr0, CHANGE); attachInterrupt(digitalPinToInterrupt(PINS[1]), isr1, CHANGE); attachInterrupt(digitalPinToInterrupt(PINS[2]), isr2, CHANGE); attachInterrupt(digitalPinToInterrupt(PINS[3]), isr3, CHANGE); } void update(uint32_t now_ms) { // call from the comms loop if (now_ms - win_start_ < 100) return; win_start_ = now_ms; portENTER_CRITICAL(&mux_); bits_ = ir::window_bits(rx_); portEXIT_CRITICAL(&mux_); } uint8_t bits() const { return bits_; } private: static const int PINS[4]; static IrBeacon* self_; static void on(int i); // in ir_beacon.cpp (IRAM) static void isr0(); static void isr1(); static void isr2(); static void isr3(); public: ir::Receiver rx_[4]; portMUX_TYPE mux_ = portMUX_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED; private: uint32_t win_start_ = 0; volatile uint8_t bits_ = 0; };

// IR beacon decoding, plain C++ (unit-tested on the PC, used by ir_beacon.h on the ESP32). // // The dock's beacon (dock/beacon_attiny85.ino) sends 38 kHz bursts, one code per LED group, round-robin: // 'A' all round : 600 us burst (4 LEDs, one per column side: "the dock is that way") // 'C' centre : 1200 us burst (1 LED in a tube, about ±6°: "you are on the dock's axis") // each followed by >= 2.4 ms of silence. A TSOP38238 pulls its output LOW for the length of a burst (±~150 us). // Per receiver we count the bursts of each code over a window; >= IR_MIN_HITS in a window = heard. #pragma once #include <stdint.h> namespace ir { constexpr uint32_t A_MIN = 380, A_MAX = 900; // us: 'A' bursts read 450-750 on a TSOP38238 constexpr uint32_t C_MIN = 950, C_MAX = 1600; // us: 'C' 1050-1350 constexpr int IR_MIN_HITS = 3; // per 100 ms window (the beacon sends ~15 of each) enum Code : uint8_t { NONE = 0, ALL_ROUND = 1, CENTRE = 2 }; inline Code classify(uint32_t low_us) { if (low_us >= A_MIN && low_us <= A_MAX) return ALL_ROUND; if (low_us >= C_MIN && low_us <= C_MAX) return CENTRE; return NONE; // noise, remote controls, sunlight flicker } struct Receiver { uint32_t fall_us = 0; bool low = false; uint16_t hits_a = 0, hits_c = 0; // one call per edge of the receiver output (level after the edge, time in us) void edge(bool level_high, uint32_t t_us) { if (!level_high) { fall_us = t_us; low = true; return; } if (!low) return; low = false; const Code c = classify(t_us - fall_us); if (c == ALL_ROUND) ++hits_a; else if (c == CENTRE) ++hits_c; } }; // 4 receivers -> 8 bits: bit 2i = receiver i heard 'A', bit 2i+1 = heard 'C'. i: 0 front-left, 1 front-right, // 2 back-left, 3 back-right. Call once per window; it resets the counters. inline uint8_t window_bits(Receiver* r, int n = 4) { uint8_t b = 0; for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) { if (r[i].hits_a >= IR_MIN_HITS) b |= 1u << (2 * i); if (r[i].hits_c >= IR_MIN_HITS) b |= 1u << (2 * i + 1); r[i].hits_a = r[i].hits_c = 0; } return b; } } // namespace ir

#include "lk_motor.h" #include <cmath> #include "sim_hil.h" bool LkMotors::begin() { #ifdef SIM_HIL simhil::begin(); return true; #endif twai_general_config_t g = TWAI_GENERAL_CONFIG_DEFAULT((gpio_num_t)PIN_CAN_TX, (gpio_num_t)PIN_CAN_RX, TWAI_MODE_NORMAL); g.tx_queue_len = 8; g.rx_queue_len = 16; twai_timing_config_t t = TWAI_TIMING_CONFIG_1MBITS(); twai_filter_config_t f = TWAI_FILTER_CONFIG_ACCEPT_ALL(); if (twai_driver_install(&g, &t, &f) != ESP_OK) return false; return twai_start() == ESP_OK; } void LkMotors::send(uint32_t id, const uint8_t d[8]) { #ifdef SIM_HIL simhil::can_tx(id, d); return; #endif twai_message_t m = {}; m.identifier = id; m.data_length_code = 8; memcpy(m.data, d, 8); if (recovering_) { ++tx_drop_count; return; } if (twai_transmit(&m, 0) != ESP_OK) ++tx_drop_count; // never block the control loop } void LkMotors::run() { const uint8_t d[8] = {0x88, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}; send(CAN_ID_LEFT, d); send(CAN_ID_RIGHT, d); } void LkMotors::off() { const uint8_t d[8] = {0x80, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}; send(CAN_ID_LEFT, d); send(CAN_ID_RIGHT, d); } static int16_t to_iq(float nm) { float iq = nm / KT / IQ_FULL_A * IQ_MAX_CMD; if (iq > IQ_MAX_CMD) iq = IQ_MAX_CMD; if (iq < -IQ_MAX_CMD) iq = -IQ_MAX_CMD; return (int16_t)lrintf(iq); } void LkMotors::torque(float left_nm, float right_nm) { const int16_t a = to_iq(DIR_LEFT * left_nm), b = to_iq(DIR_RIGHT * right_nm); // motor ID 1 = left, ID 2 = right const uint8_t d[8] = {(uint8_t)(a & 0xFF), (uint8_t)(a >> 8), (uint8_t)(b & 0xFF), (uint8_t)(b >> 8), 0, 0, 0, 0}; send(CAN_ID_MULTI, d); } void LkMotors::handle(const twai_message_t& m) { MotorState* s = nullptr; int dir = 1; if (m.identifier == CAN_ID_LEFT) { s = &left; dir = DIR_LEFT; } else if (m.identifier == CAN_ID_RIGHT) { s = &right; dir = DIR_RIGHT; } if (!s || m.data_length_code < 8) return; const uint8_t c = m.data[0]; // torque (0xA1) and state-2 (0x9C) replies carry [temp, iq, speed, encoder]; the replies to motor on/off (0x88/0x80) // only echo the command (LK manual), so they must not be parsed as state if (c != 0xA1 && c != 0x9C) return; s->temp = (int8_t)m.data[1]; const int16_t iq = (int16_t)(m.data[2] | (m.data[3] << 8)); const int16_t dps = (int16_t)(m.data[4] | (m.data[5] << 8)); const uint16_t enc = (uint16_t)(m.data[6] | (m.data[7] << 8)); // The LK manual allows a 14-, 15- or 16-bit encoder in this reply. Between two replies 2 ms apart the wheel turns at // most a few hundred counts, so a step larger than 8192 counts right after the previous reply is a wrap, and its size // tells the range. Before the first wrap, the ratio of encoder counts to the reply's own speed (dps) tells it too. // After a gap in the replies (CAN glitch) the step is unwrapped towards what the reported speed predicts instead. const uint32_t now_us = micros(); if (s->seen) { int32_t d = (int32_t)enc - (int32_t)s->enc_prev; const float dt = (now_us - s->us_prev) * 1e-6f; const bool fresh = dt > 0 && dt < 0.005f; if (!enc_locked_ && fresh && (d > 8192 || d < -8192)) { const uint32_t a = (uint32_t)(d < 0 ? -d : d); enc_range_ = a > 49152 ? 65536 : a > 24576 ? 32768 : 16384; // |d| = range - (small motion) enc_locked_ = true; enc_event = (int)enc_range_; } const float R = (float)enc_range_; const float pred = 0.5f * (dps + s->dps_prev) * dt / 360.f * R; // counts expected from the reported speed d += (int32_t)lrintf((pred - d) / R) * (int32_t)enc_range_; // whole turns that make d closest to pred if (!enc_locked_ && fresh) learn_range(d, (float)dps, dt); s->raw += d * (2.f * PI / enc_range_); } s->dps_prev = dps; s->enc_prev = enc; s->us_prev = now_us; s->seen = true; s->angle = dir * s->raw; s->speed = dir * dps * (PI / 180.f); s->current = dir * iq * IQ_FULL_A / IQ_MAX_CMD; s->last_ms = millis(); } void LkMotors::learn_range(int32_t d, float dps, float dt) { if (dt <= 0 || dt > 0.02f || std::fabs(dps) < 60.f) return; // needs real motion sum_counts_ += (float)(d < 0 ? -d : d); sum_deg_ += std::fabs(dps) * dt; if (sum_deg_ < 90.f) return; // decide after a quarter turn (motion before this is // counted at the starting guess: a one-off offset, no jump) const float per_turn = sum_counts_ / sum_deg_ * 360.f; // counts per turn const uint32_t cand[3] = {16384, 32768, 65536}; for (uint32_t c : cand) if (std::fabs(per_turn / c - 1.f) < 0.15f) { if (c != enc_range_) enc_event = (int)c; enc_range_ = c; enc_locked_ = true; return; } sum_counts_ = sum_deg_ = 0; // inconsistent (slip, noise): start over } void LkMotors::poll() { twai_message_t m; #ifdef SIM_HIL simhil::CanFrame f; simhil::pump(); while (simhil::can_rx(f)) { m = {}; m.identifier = f.id; m.data_length_code = f.dlc; memcpy(m.data, f.d, 8); handle(m); } return; #endif service(millis()); while (twai_receive(&m, 0) == ESP_OK) handle(m); } void LkMotors::service(uint32_t now) { #ifdef SIM_HIL (void)now; return; #else now_ms_ = now; twai_status_info_t st; if (twai_get_status_info(&st) != ESP_OK) return; if (st.state == TWAI_STATE_BUS_OFF && !recovering_) { // Bus-off: the controller has stopped sending. Ask for recovery (it needs 128 x 11 recessive bits, ~1.4 ms at // 1 Mbit/s, then the controller sits in STOPPED). Meanwhile nothing is sent; healthy() turns false after // CAN_TIMEOUT_MS without replies, which disarms the robot through the usual motor-fault path. recovering_ = true; bus_off_ms_ = now; ++bus_off_count; can_event = 1; twai_initiate_recovery(); } else if (recovering_ && st.state == TWAI_STATE_STOPPED) { if (twai_start() == ESP_OK) { recovering_ = false; recovered_after_ms = now - bus_off_ms_; can_event = 2; } } else if (st.state == TWAI_STATE_STOPPED && !recovering_) { twai_start(); // stopped for another reason (should not happen): start again } #endif } void LkMotors::request_state() { const uint8_t d[8] = {0x9C, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}; send(CAN_ID_LEFT, d); send(CAN_ID_RIGHT, d); } bool LkMotors::healthy(uint32_t now) const { // signed age: a reply stamped after `now` was read (same cycle) has age <= 0, not 4 billion ms const int32_t al = (int32_t)(now - left.last_ms), ar = (int32_t)(now - right.last_ms); return left.seen && right.seen && al < (int32_t)CAN_TIMEOUT_MS && ar < (int32_t)CAN_TIMEOUT_MS; }

// LK (LKMTECH) motor driver over CAN (ESP32 TWAI), torque mode. // Protocol (LK CAN V2.x): ID 0x140 + motor id. 0x88 = motor run, 0x80 = motor off, 0xA1 = torque command // (iq int16, ±2048 ≙ ±16.5 A). Multi-motor torque command: ID 0x280, 4 × int16 iq. Every motor answers with // [cmd, temp int8, iq int16, speed int16 (dps), encoder uint16]. #pragma once #include <Arduino.h> #include "driver/twai.h" #include "config.h" struct MotorState { float angle = 0; // rad, multi-turn, robot-forward positive (relative to the body) float speed = 0; // rad/s, robot-forward positive float current = 0; // A int8_t temp = 0; // °C uint32_t last_ms = 0; // last reply bool seen = false; uint16_t enc_prev = 0; uint32_t us_prev = 0; int16_t dps_prev = 0; float raw = 0; // rad, multi-turn, in the motor's own direction }; class LkMotors { public: bool begin(); void run(); // 0x88 to both void off(); // 0x80 to both (free-wheel) void torque(float left_nm, float right_nm); // one 0x280 frame void poll(); // read all pending replies void request_state(); // 0x9C (read state 2) to both: keeps speeds/encoders flowing while off bool healthy(uint32_t now_ms) const; // CAN controller health: a bus-off (too many TX errors: noise burst, loose plug, motors unpowered while sending) // stops the TWAI controller for good unless the driver restarts it. service() does that and is called by poll(). void service(uint32_t now_ms); uint32_t bus_off_count = 0; // bus-off events since boot uint32_t tx_drop_count = 0; // frames the TX queue refused (bus not acknowledging or busy) uint32_t can_event = 0; // 1 = bus-off, recovery started; 2 = recovered and restarted (main reports, then clears) uint32_t recovered_after_ms = 0; // duration of the last bus-off MotorState left, right; uint32_t enc_range() const { return enc_range_; } // counts per turn: 16384 / 32768 / 65536, detected at run time bool enc_range_known() const { return enc_locked_; } int enc_event = 0; // set when the range gets locked (main reports it once) private: uint32_t enc_range_ = (uint32_t)ENC_COUNTS; bool enc_locked_ = false; float sum_counts_ = 0, sum_deg_ = 0; // for the speed-ratio detection void learn_range(int32_t d, float dps, float dt); // Automatic power-off when the battery is flat (protects the LiPo from over-discharge). // The power switch is a Pololu Big Pushbutton Power Switch HP (#2813); its OFF input switches the robot off on a // high pulse. The push button on top always works by itself (wired straight to the switch board). // Pure logic, host-tested in test_host/test_power_off.cpp. // battery below PWR_CUTOFF_V (3.3 V/cell) for PWR_CUTOFF_MS, not charging, motors disarmed: // -> pending (telemetry flag 32: the Pi shuts down cleanly) -> PWR_GRACE_MS later: OFF pulses (200 ms every 2 s) // recovers above PWR_CUTOFF_V + 0.6 V, or a charger is connected, or it is armed -> cancelled. #pragma once #include <stdint.h> constexpr float PWR_CUTOFF_V = 19.8f; // 6 x 3.3 V constexpr uint32_t PWR_CUTOFF_MS = 30000; constexpr uint32_t PWR_GRACE_MS = 20000; // time for the Pi to halt constexpr uint32_t PWR_PULSE_MS = 200, PWR_REPULSE_MS = 2000; struct PowerOff { uint32_t below_since = 0, pending_since = 0; bool pending = false, below = false; // -> true while the OFF pin must be driven high bool step(uint32_t now, float vbat, bool charging, bool armed) { if (charging || armed || vbat > PWR_CUTOFF_V + 0.6f) { below = false; pending = false; return false; } if (vbat < PWR_CUTOFF_V) { if (!below) { below = true; below_since = now; } if (!pending && now - below_since >= PWR_CUTOFF_MS) { pending = true; pending_since = now; } } else if (!pending) below = false; // in the hysteresis band: restart the count if (!pending) return false; uint32_t t = now - pending_since; if (t < PWR_GRACE_MS) return false; return (t - PWR_GRACE_MS) % PWR_REPULSE_MS < PWR_PULSE_MS; } };

// Hardware-in-the-loop shim. -DSIM_HIL (env esp32s3_sim, QEMU): IMU + CAN over UART0. // -DBENCH_CAN (env esp32s3_bench, real ESP32 + real CAN on the bench): only the IMU comes from the PC over UART0; // the Pi's command frames share that port and are handed to `on_cmd`. // The firmware runs unchanged in Espressif QEMU; the parts QEMU does not emulate are replaced here: // - CAN (TWAI): frames go over UART0 to the physics host (virtual LK motors); console text shares the port // - IMU (I2C): each read sends a step request (with the firmware's own clock) and waits for the host's sample // The host advances the MuJoCo physics by exactly the time the firmware measured between two requests, // so the controller, its timing, the CAN protocol handling and the Pi link all run as on the robot. #pragma once #if defined(SIM_HIL) || defined(BENCH_CAN) #include <Arduino.h> #include "link_proto.h" #include "driver/uart.h" #include <algorithm> namespace simhil { constexpr uart_port_t PORT = UART_NUM_0; // shared with the console (Serial); the host separates frames from text enum : uint8_t { T_STEP = 'S', T_CAN = 'C', T_IMU = 'I' }; struct CanFrame { uint32_t id; uint8_t dlc; uint8_t d[8]; }; inline void (*on_cmd)(const uint8_t* payload, uint8_t len) = nullptr; // Pi command frames arriving on this port inline uint8_t crc(const uint8_t* p, int n) { uint8_t c = 0; while (n--) c = (uint8_t)((c << 1 | c >> 7) ^ *p++); return c; } inline void begin() { static bool done = false; if (done) return; if (!uart_is_driver_installed(PORT)) uart_driver_install(PORT, 4096, 4096, 0, nullptr, 0); // Serial.begin() normally did it uart_set_rx_full_threshold(PORT, 1); // hand every byte over at once (lock-step latency) uart_set_rx_timeout(PORT, 1); done = true; } inline void send(uint8_t type, const void* p, uint8_t len) { uint8_t b[4 + 64 + 1] = {0xA5, 0x5A, type, len}; memcpy(b + 4, p, len); b[4 + len] = crc(b + 2, 2 + len); uart_write_bytes(PORT, (const char*)b, 5 + len); } // received CAN frames, drained by LkMotors::poll() inline CanFrame rxq[32]; inline volatile int rx_head = 0, rx_tail = 0; inline bool read_exact(uint8_t* p, int n) { int got = 0; while (got < n) { const int r = uart_read_bytes(PORT, p + got, n - got, pdMS_TO_TICKS(5000)); if (r <= 0) return false; got += r; } return true; } // Send a step request and block until the host's IMU sample arrives; CAN frames received meanwhile are queued. inline bool step(uint32_t t_us, float imu[6]) { send(T_STEP, &t_us, 4); for (;;) { uint8_t h[4]; if (!read_exact(h, 1)) return false; if (h[0] != 0xA5) continue; if (!read_exact(h + 1, 3) || h[1] != 0x5A) continue; uint8_t p[64 + 1]; if (h[3] > 64 || !read_exact(p, h[3] + 1)) continue; uint8_t chk[66]; chk[0] = h[2]; chk[1] = h[3]; memcpy(chk + 2, p, h[3]); if (h[2] == pilink::MSG_CMD) { // Pi link frame (its own CRC) if (pilink::crc8(chk, 2 + h[3]) == p[h[3]] && on_cmd) on_cmd(p, h[3]); continue; } if (crc(chk, 2 + h[3]) != p[h[3]]) continue; if (h[2] == T_CAN && h[3] == sizeof(CanFrame)) { const int nx = (rx_head + 1) % 32; if (nx != rx_tail) { memcpy(&rxq[rx_head], p, sizeof(CanFrame)); rx_head = nx; } } else if (h[2] == T_IMU && h[3] == 24) { memcpy(imu, p, 24); return true; } } } // Non-blocking: parse whatever bytes already arrived (motor replies to the last command), as the TWAI RX FIFO would hold them. inline void pump() { static uint8_t buf[256]; static int n = 0; size_t avail = 0; uart_get_buffered_data_len(PORT, &avail); while (avail > 0) { const int r = uart_read_bytes(PORT, buf + n, (int)std::min<size_t>(avail, sizeof(buf) - n), 0); if (r <= 0) break; n += r; avail -= r; for (;;) { int i = 0; while (i + 1 < n && !(buf[i] == 0xA5 && buf[i + 1] == 0x5A)) ++i; if (i) { memmove(buf, buf + i, n - i); n -= i; } if (n < 4) break; const int need = 4 + buf[3] + 1; if (buf[3] > 64) { memmove(buf, buf + 2, n - 2); n -= 2; continue; } if (n < need) break; if (crc(buf + 2, 2 + buf[3]) == buf[need - 1] && buf[2] == T_CAN && buf[3] == sizeof(CanFrame)) { const int nx = (rx_head + 1) % 32; if (nx != rx_tail) { memcpy(&rxq[rx_head], buf + 4, sizeof(CanFrame)); rx_head = nx; } } memmove(buf, buf + need, n - need); n -= need; } if (n == (int)sizeof(buf)) n = 0; } } inline void can_tx(uint32_t id, const uint8_t d[8]) { CanFrame f{}; f.id = id; f.dlc = 8; memcpy(f.d, d, 8); send(T_CAN, &f, sizeof f); } inline bool can_rx(CanFrame& f) { if (rx_tail == rx_head) return false; f = rxq[rx_tail]; rx_tail = (rx_tail + 1) % 32; return true; } } // namespace simhil #endif

#include "sonar.h" Sonar* Sonar::self_ = nullptr; void IRAM_ATTR Sonar::isr() { const uint32_t t = micros(); if (digitalRead(PIN_SONAR_ECHO)) self_->rise_ = t; else { const uint32_t us = t - self_->rise_; self_->dist_ = (us > 100 && us < 25000) ? us * 343e-6f / 2.f : -1.f; // 2 cm .. 4.3 m self_->waiting_ = false; } }

// HC-SR04, non-blocking: trigger every 60 ms, measure the echo with a pin-change interrupt. #pragma once #include <Arduino.h> #include "config.h" class Sonar { public: void begin() { pinMode(PIN_SONAR_TRIG, OUTPUT); digitalWrite(PIN_SONAR_TRIG, LOW); pinMode(PIN_SONAR_ECHO, INPUT); self_ = this; attachInterrupt(digitalPinToInterrupt(PIN_SONAR_ECHO), isr, CHANGE); } void update(uint32_t now_ms) { // call from the main loop if (now_ms - last_trig_ >= 60) { if (waiting_) dist_ = -1; // previous echo never ended: nothing in range last_trig_ = now_ms; waiting_ = true; digitalWrite(PIN_SONAR_TRIG, HIGH); delayMicroseconds(10); digitalWrite(PIN_SONAR_TRIG, LOW); } } float distance() const { return dist_; } // m, -1 = none private: static void isr(); static Sonar* self_; public: volatile uint32_t rise_ = 0; volatile float dist_ = -1; volatile bool waiting_ = false; private: uint32_t last_trig_ = 0; };

// VL53L5CX: 8 x 8 zones, 45 x 45 deg, on its own I2C bus. The alternative to the HC-SR04. // // What this turns 64 ranges into, for the controller: // obstacle_m - the nearest return that is NOT the floor, i.e. something standing in the way. // drop_m - how far ahead the floor stops. A sonar cannot produce this at all: its cone reports // one range with no bearing, so "the floor echo is gone" says nothing about where. // Each zone here has a known elevation, so the range the floor SHOULD return in that // zone is h / sin(tilt + elevation + pitch) - exact geometry, no calibration - and the // first row whose return is much longer than that is looking past the edge. // // The ST ULD API (STSW-IMG023) is not vendored here: it is ~90 kB of ST-licensed C. Add it through // platformio (lib_deps = stm32duino/VL53L5CX) or drop the ULD sources into lib/vl53l5cx/, then build // with -D FRONT_SENSOR=FRONT_TOF -D HAS_VL53L5CX=1. Without it this file still compiles and reports // nothing, so a board with no sensor fitted behaves exactly as before. #pragma once #include <Arduino.h> #include <math.h> #include "config.h" #if HAS_VL53L5CX #include <vl53l5cx_api.h> #endif class Tof { public: static constexpr int N = 8; // zones per side static constexpr float FLOOR_TOL = 0.080f; // m: longer than predicted floor = past the edge bool begin() { #if HAS_VL53L5CX pinMode(PIN_TOF_LPN, OUTPUT); digitalWrite(PIN_TOF_LPN, LOW); // held in reset while the bus comes up delay(10); digitalWrite(PIN_TOF_LPN, HIGH); cfg_.platform.address = 0x52; cfg_.platform.sda = PIN_TOF_SDA; cfg_.platform.scl = PIN_TOF_SCL; cfg_.platform.freq_hz = 1000000; // its own bus: the IMU's is capped at 400 kHz uint8_t alive = 0; if (vl53l5cx_is_alive(&cfg_, &alive) || !alive) return false; if (vl53l5cx_init(&cfg_)) return false; // ~84 kB of firmware over I2C: ~1.4 s at 1 MHz vl53l5cx_set_resolution(&cfg_, VL53L5CX_RESOLUTION_8X8); vl53l5cx_set_ranging_frequency_hz(&cfg_, 15); // 8x8 is capped at 15 Hz; 4x4 would allow 60 vl53l5cx_set_ranging_mode(&cfg_, VL53L5CX_RANGING_MODE_CONTINUOUS); return vl53l5cx_start_ranging(&cfg_) == 0; #else return false; #endif } // Call from the slow loop. `pitch` is the body pitch in rad, nose-down positive, from the IMU: // the array is bolted to the body, so every zone's elevation moves with it. void update(float pitch) { #if HAS_VL53L5CX uint8_t ready = 0; if (vl53l5cx_check_data_ready(&cfg_, &ready) || !ready) return; if (vl53l5cx_get_ranging_data(&cfg_, &res_)) return; float obstacle = -1, drop = -1; for (int row = 0; row < N; ++row) { const float el = radians(TOF_TILT_DEG) + (row - (N - 1) / 2.0f) * radians(TOF_FOV_DEG) / N; const float a = el + pitch; const float floor_m = (a > radians(3.0f)) ? TOF_HEIGHT_M / sinf(a) : 1e9f; for (int col = 0; col < N; ++col) { const int i = row * N + col; if ((res_.target_status[VL53L5CX_NB_TARGET_PER_ZONE * i] != 5) && (res_.target_status[VL53L5CX_NB_TARGET_PER_ZONE * i] != 9)) continue; // 5/9 = valid const float r = res_.distance_mm[VL53L5CX_NB_TARGET_PER_ZONE * i] / 1000.0f; if (r < 0.02f || r > 4.0f) continue; if (r < floor_m - FLOOR_TOL) { // nearer than the floor: something is there if (obstacle < 0 || r < obstacle) obstacle = r; } else if (r > floor_m + FLOOR_TOL) { // further than the floor: the floor ran out const float horiz = r * cosf(a); // where that ray would have met floor level const float edge = floor_m * cosf(a); const float d = fminf(edge, horiz); if (drop < 0 || d < drop) drop = d; } } } obstacle_ = obstacle; drop_ = drop; fresh_ = true; #else (void)pitch; #endif } float obstacle_m() const { return obstacle_; } // m, < 0 = nothing float drop_m() const { return drop_; } // m, < 0 = no edge seen bool fresh() const { return fresh_; } private: float obstacle_ = -1, drop_ = -1; bool fresh_ = false; #if HAS_VL53L5CX VL53L5CX_Configuration cfg_{}; VL53L5CX_ResultsData res_{}; #endif };

#!/bin/bash # Build and run the PC unit tests of the CAN motor code (needs g++ with C++17). set -e cd "$(dirname "$0")" g++ -std=gnu++17 -O1 -Wall -Wno-unused-function -I fake -I ../include -I ../src test_lk_motor.cpp ../src/lk_motor.cpp -o /tmp/test_lk_motor /tmp/test_lk_motor g++ -std=gnu++17 -O1 -Wall -I ../src test_ir_decode.cpp -o /tmp/test_ir_decode /tmp/test_ir_decode g++ -std=gnu++17 -O1 -Wall -I ../src test_power_off.cpp -o /tmp/test_power_off /tmp/test_power_off g++ -std=gnu++17 -O1 -Wall -I fake -I ../include -I ../src test_tof.cpp -o /tmp/test_tof /tmp/test_tof g++ -std=gnu++17 -O1 -Wall ../../dock_beacon/test_dock_logic.cpp -o /tmp/test_dock_logic /tmp/test_dock_logic

// PC test of the IR beacon decoder (src/ir_decode.h). #include <cstdio> #include "ir_decode.h" static int fails = 0, checks = 0; #define CHECK(c) do { ++checks; if (!(c)) { ++fails; std::printf("FAIL %s:%d %s\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #c); } } while (0) static void burst(ir::Receiver& r, uint32_t& t, uint32_t low_us, uint32_t gap_us) { r.edge(false, t); t += low_us; r.edge(true, t); t += gap_us; } int main() { CHECK(ir::classify(600) == ir::ALL_ROUND); CHECK(ir::classify(1200) == ir::CENTRE); CHECK(ir::classify(200) == ir::NONE); CHECK(ir::classify(920) == ir::NONE); CHECK(ir::classify(2500) == ir::NONE); ir::Receiver rx[4]; uint32_t t = 1000; for (int k = 0; k < 15; ++k) { burst(rx[2], t, 640, 2400); burst(rx[2], t, 1180, 2400); } // back-left: both codes for (int k = 0; k < 15; ++k) burst(rx[1], t, 560, 2400); // front-right: all round only for (int k = 0; k < 2; ++k) burst(rx[0], t, 600, 2400); // front-left: too few for (int k = 0; k < 20; ++k) burst(rx[3], t, 9000, 4500); // back-right: a TV remote's header const uint8_t b = ir::window_bits(rx); CHECK(b == ((1u << 4) | (1u << 5) | (1u << 2))); CHECK(ir::window_bits(rx) == 0); // counters reset each window rx[0].edge(true, t); // a rising edge without a fall is ignored CHECK(rx[0].hits_a == 0 && rx[0].hits_c == 0); std::printf("%d checks, %d failed\n", checks, fails); return fails ? 1 : 0; }

// Unit tests for src/lk_motor.cpp (LK MF6015 CAN protocol), built on the PC against a fake TWAI driver. // Run: ./run_tests.sh #include <cstdio> #include <cmath> #include <string> #include "lk_motor.h" static int fails = 0, checks = 0; #define CHECK(cond, ...) do { ++checks; if (!(cond)) { ++fails; std::printf(" FAIL %s:%d ", __FILE__, __LINE__); std::printf(__VA_ARGS__); std::printf("\n"); } } while (0) #define NEAR(a, b, tol) (std::fabs((double)(a) - (double)(b)) <= (tol)) static void reset() { fake::tx.clear(); fake::rx.clear(); fake::us = 1000000; fake::tx_queue_free = 1000; fake::installed = false; fake::started = false; fake::state = TWAI_STATE_STOPPED; fake::recoveries = fake::starts = 0; } // LK reply [cmd, temp, iq lo/hi, dps lo/hi, enc lo/hi] from motor `id` static void reply(uint32_t id, uint8_t cmd, int8_t temp, int16_t iq, int16_t dps, uint16_t enc, uint8_t dlc = 8) { twai_message_t m{}; m.identifier = id; m.data_length_code = dlc; const uint8_t d[8] = {cmd, (uint8_t)temp, (uint8_t)(iq & 0xFF), (uint8_t)((uint16_t)iq >> 8), (uint8_t)(dps & 0xFF), (uint8_t)((uint16_t)dps >> 8), (uint8_t)(enc & 0xFF), (uint8_t)(enc >> 8)}; memcpy(m.data, d, 8); fake::rx.push_back(m); } static int16_t i16(const uint8_t* p) { return (int16_t)(p[0] | (p[1] << 8)); } // spin one motor at `dps` (its own direction) with an encoder of `bits`, `n` replies 2 ms apart, starting at enc0 static uint16_t spin(LkMotors& mm, uint32_t id, int bits, float dps, int n, double& enc_f) { const double range = (double)(1 << bits); uint16_t e = 0; for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) { enc_f += dps * 0.002 / 360.0 * range; double w = std::fmod(enc_f, range); if (w < 0) w += range; e = (uint16_t)((uint32_t)std::lround(w) % (uint32_t)range); reply(id, 0xA1, 30, 0, (int16_t)std::lround(dps), e); fake::us += 2000; mm.poll(); } return e; } static void test_commands() { std::printf("commands\n"); reset(); LkMotors m; CHECK(m.begin(), "begin"); m.run(); CHECK(fake::tx.size() == 2 && fake::tx[0].identifier == CAN_ID_LEFT && fake::tx[1].identifier == CAN_ID_RIGHT, "run -> 2 frames to 0x141/0x142"); CHECK(fake::tx[0].data[0] == 0x88 && fake::tx[0].data_length_code == 8, "run = 0x88, DLC 8"); fake::tx.clear(); m.off(); CHECK(fake::tx.size() == 2 && fake::tx[0].data[0] == 0x80 && fake::tx[1].data[0] == 0x80, "off = 0x80 to both"); fake::tx.clear(); m.request_state(); CHECK(fake::tx.size() == 2 && fake::tx[0].data[0] == 0x9C, "request_state = 0x9C"); } static void test_torque_packing() { std::printf("torque packing (0x280)\n"); reset(); LkMotors m; m.begin(); m.torque(0.2f, 0.2f); CHECK(fake::tx.size() == 1 && fake::tx[0].identifier == CAN_ID_MULTI, "one 0x280 frame"); const int16_t a = i16(fake::tx[0].data), b = i16(fake::tx[0].data + 2); const int expect = (int)std::lround(0.2 / KT / IQ_FULL_A * IQ_MAX_CMD); // 177 CHECK(a == DIR_LEFT * expect, "left iq %d, expected %d (motor 1 in bytes 0-1)", a, DIR_LEFT * expect); CHECK(b == DIR_RIGHT * expect, "right iq %d, expected %d (motor 2 in bytes 2-3, mirrored)", b, DIR_RIGHT * expect); CHECK(i16(fake::tx[0].data + 4) == 0 && i16(fake::tx[0].data + 6) == 0, "motors 3/4 slots zero"); fake::tx.clear(); m.torque(50.f, -50.f); CHECK(i16(fake::tx[0].data) == DIR_LEFT * IQ_MAX_CMD && i16(fake::tx[0].data + 2) == -DIR_RIGHT * IQ_MAX_CMD, "clamped to +-2048"); fake::tx.clear(); m.torque(-0.0001f, 0.0001f); CHECK(i16(fake::tx[0].data) == 0 && i16(fake::tx[0].data + 2) == 0, "tiny torque rounds to 0"); } static void test_reply_parsing() { std::printf("reply parsing\n"); reset(); LkMotors m; m.begin(); reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0xA1, 42, 1024, 360, 0); reply(CAN_ID_RIGHT, 0x9C, -5, -1024, -720, 0); m.poll(); CHECK(m.left.seen && m.right.seen, "both seen"); CHECK(m.left.temp == 42 && m.right.temp == -5, "temperature int8"); CHECK(NEAR(m.left.current, DIR_LEFT * 8.25f, 1e-3), "left current %.3f A (1024 = 8.25 A)", m.left.current); CHECK(NEAR(m.right.current, DIR_RIGHT * -8.25f, 1e-3), "right current %.3f A, direction applied", m.right.current); CHECK(NEAR(m.left.speed, DIR_LEFT * 2 * PI, 1e-4), "left 360 dps = 2 pi rad/s (%.4f)", m.left.speed); CHECK(NEAR(m.right.speed, DIR_RIGHT * -4 * PI, 1e-4), "right -720 dps with direction (%.4f)", m.right.speed); CHECK(m.left.last_ms == millis(), "timestamped"); } static void test_ignored_frames() { std::printf("frames that must not change the state\n"); reset(); LkMotors m; m.begin(); reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0xA1, 30, 100, 90, 1000); m.poll(); const MotorState before = m.left; fake::us += 5000; reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0x88, 0, 0, 0, 0); // motor-on echo (LK manual: reply = the command) reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0x80, 0, 0, 0, 0); // motor-off echo reply(0x143, 0xA1, 0, 0, 0, 0); // other motor ID reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0xA1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 6); // short frame m.poll(); CHECK(m.left.angle == before.angle && m.left.speed == before.speed && m.left.last_ms == before.last_ms, "0x88/0x80 echoes, foreign IDs and short frames ignored"); } static void test_unwrap(int bits, float dps, const char* what) { reset(); LkMotors m; m.begin(); double enc = 1000.0; reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0xA1, 30, 0, 0, 1000); m.poll(); int i = 0; float a_lock = 0; int i_lock = -1; for (; i < 3000; ++i) { // 6 s, one reply every 2 ms spin(m, CAN_ID_LEFT, bits, dps, 1, enc); if (i_lock < 0 && m.enc_range_known()) { i_lock = i; a_lock = m.left.angle; } } CHECK(m.enc_range_known() && m.enc_range() == (1u << bits), "%s: range %u detected (expected %u)", what, m.enc_range(), 1u << bits); const float after = DIR_LEFT * dps * 0.002f * (i - 1 - i_lock) * PI / 180.f; CHECK(i_lock >= 0 && NEAR(m.left.angle - a_lock, after, 0.01), "%s: exact after detection: %.3f rad, expected %.3f", what, m.left.angle - a_lock, after); const float total = DIR_LEFT * dps * 0.002f * i * PI / 180.f; CHECK(std::fabs(m.left.angle - total) < 0.75f * PI / 2 + 0.02f, "%s: one-off offset %.2f rad (bound: 3/4 of the 90 deg learning window)", what, m.left.angle - total); } static void test_ranges() { std::printf("encoder unwrap + range detection\n"); for (int bits : {14, 15, 16}) { char w[40]; std::snprintf(w, sizeof w, "%d-bit forward", bits); test_unwrap(bits, 720.f, w); std::snprintf(w, sizeof w, "%d-bit reverse", bits); test_unwrap(bits, -900.f, w); } } static void test_ratio_before_wrap() { std::printf("range from the speed ratio, before any wrap\n"); for (int bits : {14, 15, 16}) { reset(); LkMotors m; m.begin(); double enc = 10.0; reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0xA1, 30, 0, 0, 10); m.poll(); spin(m, CAN_ID_LEFT, bits, 400.f, 260, enc); // 208 deg: no wrap yet (starts near 0) CHECK(m.enc_range_known() && m.enc_range() == (1u << bits), "%d-bit: %u", bits, m.enc_range()); CHECK(m.enc_event == (bits == 16 ? 0 : (1 << bits)), "%d-bit: event %d", bits, m.enc_event); } reset(); LkMotors m; m.begin(); double enc = 10.0; reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0xA1, 30, 0, 0, 10); m.poll(); spin(m, CAN_ID_LEFT, 16, 30.f, 2000, enc); // too slow to learn from CHECK(!m.enc_range_known(), "slow motion (30 dps) does not lock the range"); } static void test_reply_gap() { std::printf("replies missing for a while (CAN glitch) while the wheel keeps turning\n"); reset(); LkMotors m; m.begin(); double enc = 1000.0; reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0xA1, 30, 0, 0, 1000); m.poll(); spin(m, CAN_ID_LEFT, 16, 720.f, 400, enc); // locks 65536 on the way CHECK(m.enc_range() == 65536, "locked 16-bit first (%u)", m.enc_range()); const float a0 = m.left.angle; enc += 720.0 * 0.100 / 360.0 * 65536; fake::us += 100000; // 100 ms without replies: 72 deg = 13107 counts spin(m, CAN_ID_LEFT, 16, 720.f, 50, enc); CHECK(m.enc_range() == 65536, "a gap must not change the detected range (now %u)", m.enc_range()); const float exp = DIR_LEFT * (720.f * 0.100f + 720.f * 0.002f * 50) * PI / 180.f; CHECK(NEAR(m.left.angle - a0, exp, 0.05), "angle across the gap %.3f, expected %.3f", m.left.angle - a0, exp); } static void test_healthy() { std::printf("health / CAN timeout\n"); reset(); LkMotors m; m.begin(); CHECK(!m.healthy(millis()), "nothing seen -> unhealthy"); reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0xA1, 30, 0, 0, 0); m.poll(); CHECK(!m.healthy(millis()), "one motor only -> unhealthy"); reply(CAN_ID_RIGHT, 0xA1, 30, 0, 0, 0); m.poll(); CHECK(m.healthy(millis()), "both fresh -> healthy"); CHECK(m.healthy(millis() - 1), "reply stamped after `now` (age -1 ms) -> healthy (was a wrap-around bug)"); CHECK(m.healthy(millis() + CAN_TIMEOUT_MS - 1), "age %u ms -> healthy", (unsigned)CAN_TIMEOUT_MS - 1); CHECK(!m.healthy(millis() + CAN_TIMEOUT_MS), "age %u ms -> timeout", (unsigned)CAN_TIMEOUT_MS); } static void test_tx_full() { std::printf("full TX queue never blocks\n"); reset(); LkMotors m; m.begin(); fake::tx_queue_free = 0; m.torque(1.f, 1.f); m.run(); m.off(); CHECK(fake::tx.empty(), "frames dropped, call returned"); } static void test_bus_off() { std::printf("CAN bus-off -> recovery -> restart\n"); reset(); LkMotors m; m.begin(); CHECK(fake::state == TWAI_STATE_RUNNING, "running after begin"); reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0xA1, 30, 0, 0, 0); reply(CAN_ID_RIGHT, 0xA1, 30, 0, 0, 0); m.poll(); CHECK(m.healthy(millis()), "healthy before"); fake::state = TWAI_STATE_BUS_OFF; // e.g. a noise burst: TX error counter > 255 fake::tx.clear(); m.torque(0.5f, 0.5f); CHECK(fake::tx.empty() && m.tx_drop_count == 1, "frame refused while bus-off, counted (%u)", m.tx_drop_count); fake::us += 1000; m.poll(); CHECK(fake::recoveries == 1 && m.bus_off_count == 1 && m.can_event == 1, "recovery requested once, event 1"); m.can_event = 0; m.torque(0.5f, 0.5f); CHECK(fake::tx.empty(), "nothing sent while recovering"); fake::us += 1000; m.poll(); // fake: recovery done -> STOPPED fake::us += 1000; m.poll(); // driver restarts the controller CHECK(fake::state == TWAI_STATE_RUNNING && m.can_event == 2, "controller restarted, event 2 (state %d)", (int)fake::state); CHECK(m.recovered_after_ms >= 1 && m.recovered_after_ms <= 5, "outage %u ms", m.recovered_after_ms); CHECK(fake::recoveries == 1, "recovery not requested twice (%d)", fake::recoveries); fake::tx.clear(); m.torque(0.5f, 0.5f); CHECK(fake::tx.size() == 1, "sending again after recovery"); reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0xA1, 30, 0, 0, 0); reply(CAN_ID_RIGHT, 0xA1, 30, 0, 0, 0); m.poll(); CHECK(m.healthy(millis()), "healthy again once replies return"); // a second bus-off is handled the same way fake::state = TWAI_STATE_BUS_OFF; m.poll(); m.poll(); m.poll(); m.poll(); CHECK(m.bus_off_count == 2 && fake::state == TWAI_STATE_RUNNING, "second bus-off recovered (count %u)", m.bus_off_count); } static void test_bus_off_long() { std::printf("bus-off longer than the CAN timeout -> motor fault (disarm), then recovers\n"); reset(); LkMotors m; m.begin(); reply(CAN_ID_LEFT, 0xA1, 30, 0, 0, 0); reply(CAN_ID_RIGHT, 0xA1, 30, 0, 0, 0); m.poll(); fake::state = TWAI_STATE_BUS_OFF; m.poll(); fake::recover_polls = 1000000; // recovery stuck (bus shorted) for (int i = 0; i < 30; ++i) { fake::us += 2000; m.poll(); } CHECK(!m.healthy(millis()), "no replies for 60 ms -> unhealthy -> main disarms"); CHECK(fake::recoveries == 1, "no recovery spam while stuck (%d)", fake::recoveries); fake::recover_polls = 1; m.poll(); m.poll(); CHECK(fake::state == TWAI_STATE_RUNNING, "restarts when the bus clears"); } int main() { test_commands(); test_torque_packing(); test_reply_parsing(); test_ignored_frames(); test_ranges(); test_ratio_before_wrap(); test_reply_gap(); test_healthy(); test_tx_full(); test_bus_off(); test_bus_off_long(); std::printf("\n%d checks, %d failed\n", checks, fails); return fails ? 1 : 0; }

// Host test of the flat-battery power-off logic (src/power_off.h). #include <cstdio> #include "../src/power_off.h" static int checks = 0, fails = 0; #define CHECK(c, m) do { ++checks; if (!(c)) { ++fails; printf("FAIL: %s\n", m); } } while (0) static bool run(PowerOff &p, uint32_t &t, uint32_t ms, float v, bool chg, bool armed, uint32_t *first_high = nullptr) { bool any = false; for (uint32_t k = 0; k < ms; k += 10, t += 10) { bool h = p.step(t, v, chg, armed); if (h && !any && first_high) *first_high = t; any |= h; } return any; } int main() { { PowerOff p; uint32_t t = 0; CHECK(!run(p, t, 600000, 22.5f, false, false), "healthy battery: never off"); } { PowerOff p; uint32_t t = 0, fh = 0; CHECK(run(p, t, 60000, 19.5f, false, false, &fh), "flat battery: switches off"); CHECK(fh >= PWR_CUTOFF_MS + PWR_GRACE_MS && fh < PWR_CUTOFF_MS + PWR_GRACE_MS + 50, "after 30 s + 20 s grace"); CHECK(p.pending, "pending flag for the Pi"); } { PowerOff p; uint32_t t = 0; CHECK(!run(p, t, 120000, 19.5f, true, false), "charging: never off"); } { PowerOff p; uint32_t t = 0; CHECK(!run(p, t, 120000, 19.5f, false, true), "armed (balancing): never cut, it disarms first"); } { PowerOff p; uint32_t t = 0; run(p, t, 35000, 19.5f, false, false); CHECK(p.pending, "pending after 35 s"); CHECK(!run(p, t, 60000, 20.6f, false, false) && !p.pending, "recovers above 20.4 V: cancelled"); } { PowerOff p; uint32_t t = 0; // brief dips (motor load) don't add up bool off = false; for (int i = 0; i < 40; ++i) { off |= run(p, t, 5000, 19.5f, false, false); off |= run(p, t, 1000, 20.5f, false, false); } CHECK(!off, "dips of 5 s separated by recovery: no power-off"); } { PowerOff p; uint32_t t = 0; uint32_t highs = 0; run(p, t, PWR_CUTOFF_MS + PWR_GRACE_MS, 19.5f, false, false); for (int i = 0; i < 1000; ++i, t += 10) if (p.step(t, 19.5f, false, false)) highs += 10; CHECK(highs >= 900 && highs <= 1100, "OFF pulses 200 ms every 2 s"); } printf("%d checks, %d failed\n", checks, fails); return fails ? 1 : 0; }

// Compiles the zone-array driver the way a board with no sensor library would: the guard must leave a // class that still builds and reports nothing. #include "tof.h" #include <cstdio> static int checks = 0, failed = 0; static void ck(bool c, const char* what) { ++checks; if (!c) { ++failed; printf("FAIL: %s\n", what); } } int main() { Tof t; // Without the ST ULD library linked in, the driver must still build and must report "nothing" - // never a stale or default distance. A board with no sensor fitted has to behave exactly as before. ck(!t.begin(), "begin() fails when no sensor library is linked"); t.update(0.0f); ck(t.obstacle_m() < 0, "obstacle_m is negative (unknown), not 0"); ck(t.drop_m() < 0, "drop_m is negative (unknown): the fence must not arm on a missing sensor"); ck(!t.fresh(), "no frame is reported fresh"); ck(Tof::N == 8, "8 x 8 zones"); printf("%d checks, %d failed\n", checks, failed); return failed ? 1 : 0; }

#include "controller.hpp" #include "standup_policy.hpp" #include "gains.hpp" #include <cmath> #include <algorithm> namespace bot { namespace { constexpr float PI = 3.14159265f; inline float clampf(float v, float lo, float hi) { return v < lo ? lo : (v > hi ? hi : v); } inline float wrap(float a) { // -> (-pi, pi] while (a > PI) a -= 2 * PI; while (a <= -PI) a += 2 * PI; return a; } inline float slew(float cur, float target, float rate, float dt) { float d = target - cur, m = rate * dt; return cur + clampf(d, -m, m); } // Stand-up / safety thresholds constexpr float LYING_PITCH = 0.60f; // rad (34°): beyond this at arm time we treat it as lying constexpr float FALL_PITCH = 0.85f; // rad (49°): balancing lost constexpr float SIDE_ROLL = 0.80f; // rad (46°): lying on its side, cannot stand up constexpr float LIFT_TIMEOUT = 1.2f; // s constexpr float STILL_RATE = 0.6f; // rad/s: "not moving" while lying constexpr float WHEEL_W_MAX = 120.f; // rad/s: no-load speed at 22 V (53 rpm/V); // CAN bench probe (env esp32s3_canprobe). Flash it instead of the robot firmware, open the serial monitor // (pio device monitor -e esp32s3_canprobe), follow the prompts. // // 1. Transceiver self-test: TWAI in no-ACK mode sends frames to itself THROUGH the SN65HVD230 (needs only the CAN board, // no motor, no other node). 20/20 received = ESP32 <-> CAN board wiring OK. 0 = CTX/CRX swapped, no 3.3 V, bad joint. // 2. Bus scan: 0x9C "read state 2" to motor IDs 1-4 every 200 ms, decoded replies + bus error counters. // 3. Keys: 1/2 select motor ID, r = motor on (0x88), o = off (0x80), + / - = +-0.2 N·m for 0.5 s (wheels OFF the ground), // e = encoder range test (turn the wheel slowly by hand, one full turn), s = status, h = help. #include <Arduino.h> #include "driver/twai.h" #include "config.h" static uint8_t sel = 1; static bool install(twai_mode_t mode) { twai_general_config_t g = TWAI_GENERAL_CONFIG_DEFAULT((gpio_num_t)PIN_CAN_TX, (gpio_num_t)PIN_CAN_RX, mode); g.tx_queue_len = 16; g.rx_queue_len = 32; twai_timing_config_t t = TWAI_TIMING_CONFIG_1MBITS(); twai_filter_config_t f = TWAI_FILTER_CONFIG_ACCEPT_ALL(); return twai_driver_install(&g, &t, &f) == ESP_OK && twai_start() == ESP_OK; } static void uninstall() { twai_stop(); twai_driver_uninstall(); } static void status(const char* tag) { twai_status_info_t s; twai_get_status_info(&s); static const char* st[] = {"STOPPED", "RUNNING", "BUS_OFF", "RECOVERING"}; Serial.printf("[%s] state %s tx_err %u rx_err %u tx_failed %u bus_errors %u arb_lost %u rx_missed %u\n", tag, st[s.state & 3], s.tx_error_counter, s.rx_error_counter, s.tx_failed_count, s.bus_error_count, s.arb_lost_count, s.rx_missed_count); } static void send(uint32_t id, const uint8_t d[8]) { twai_message_t m = {}; m.identifier = id; m.data_length_code = 8; memcpy(m.data, d, 8); if (twai_transmit(&m, pdMS_TO_TICKS(5)) != ESP_OK) Serial.printf(" tx 0x%03X failed\n", (unsigned)id); } static void self_test() { Serial.println("\n== 1. transceiver self-test (no-ACK, self-reception, 1 Mbit/s) =="); if (!install(TWAI_MODE_NO_ACK)) { Serial.println("TWAI install failed"); return; } int ok = 0; for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) { twai_message_t m = {}; m.identifier = 0x7A0 + i; m.data_length_code = 8; m.flags = TWAI_MSG_FLAG_SELF; for (int k = 0; k < 8; ++k) m.data[k] = (uint8_t)(i * 13 + k); if (twai_transmit(&m, pdMS_TO_TICKS(20)) != ESP_OK) continue; twai_message_t r; if (twai_receive(&r, pdMS_TO_TICKS(20)) == ESP_OK && r.identifier == m.identifier && !memcmp(r.data, m.data, 8)) ++ok; } status("self-test"); Serial.printf("self-test: %d/20 frames came back through the transceiver -> %s\n", ok, ok == 20 ? "ESP32 <-> CAN board OK" : ok == 0 ? "NOTHING: check CTX->GPIO%d, CRX->GPIO%d (not swapped), 3.3 V and GND on the CAN board" : "PARTIAL: loose joint or noise"); uninstall(); } static void decode(const twai_message_t& m) { const uint8_t c = m.data[0]; if (c == 0x9C || c == 0xA1) { const int16_t iq = (int16_t)(m.data[2] | (m.data[3] << 8)), dps = (int16_t)(m.data[4] | (m.data[5] << 8)); const uint16_t enc = (uint16_t)(m.data[6] | (m.data[7] << 8)); Serial.printf(" motor %u: %s temp %d C iq %.2f A speed %d dps enc %u\n", (unsigned)(m.identifier - 0x140), c == 0x9C ? "state" : "torque", (int8_t)m.data[1], iq * IQ_FULL_A / IQ_MAX_CMD, dps, enc); } else { Serial.printf(" 0x%03X: %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X\n", (unsigned)m.identifier, m.data[0], m.data[1], m.data[2], m.data[3], m.data[4], m.data[5], m.data[6], m.data[7]); } } static void scan(bool print) { const uint8_t d[8] = {0x9C, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}; bool seen[5] = {}; for (int id = 1; id <= 4; ++id) send(0x140 + id, d); const uint32_t t0 = millis(); twai_message_t m; while (millis() - t0 < 20) if (twai_receive(&m, pdMS_TO_TICKS(2)) == ESP_OK) { if (m.identifier > 0x140 && m.identifier <= 0x144) seen[m.identifier - 0x140] = true; if (print) decode(m); } if (print) { Serial.printf(" answering IDs:"); for (int id = 1; id <= 4; ++id) if (seen[id]) Serial.printf(" %d", id); Serial.println(seen[1] || seen[2] || seen[3] || seen[4] ? "" : " none (motor powered? ID/baud set to 1/2 @ 1 Mbit/s? H/L swapped? 60 ohm?)"); } } static void torque_test(float nm) { const int16_t iq = (int16_t)lrintf(nm / KT / IQ_FULL_A * IQ_MAX_CMD); Serial.printf("\nmotor %u: %+.2f N·m (iq %d) for 0.5 s -- wheel must be OFF the ground\n", sel, nm, iq); const uint8_t on[8] = {0x88, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}, off[8] = {0x80, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}; const uint8_t t[8] = {0xA1, 0, 0, 0, (uint8_t)(iq & 0xFF), (uint8_t)((uint16_t)iq >> 8), 0, 0}; send(0x140 + sel, on); int32_t sum_dps = 0; int n = 0; for (uint32_t t0 = millis(); millis() - t0 < 500;) { send(0x140 + sel, t); twai_message_t m; while (twai_receive(&m, pdMS_TO_TICKS(1)) == ESP_OK) if (m.identifier == 0x140u + sel && m.data[0] == 0xA1) { sum_dps += (int16_t)(m.data[4] | (m.data[5] << 8)); ++n; } delay(2); } send(0x140 + sel, off); const int avg = n ? sum_dps / n : 0; Serial.printf(" %d replies, mean speed %d dps (motor's own sign)\n", n, avg); Serial.printf(" -> look at the wheel: did it turn so the ROBOT would roll FORWARD? If yes, set %s = %+d in config.h," " otherwise %+d. (Positive command gave %s speed.)\n", sel == 1 ? "DIR_LEFT" : "DIR_RIGHT", nm > 0 ? 1 : -1, nm > 0 ? -1 : 1, avg > 0 ? "positive" : avg < 0 ? "negative" : "no"); } static void encoder_test() { Serial.printf("\nmotor %u encoder: turn the wheel slowly by hand, about one full turn, within 10 s...\n", sel); const uint8_t d[8] = {0x9C, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}; uint16_t lo = 65535, hi = 0; int32_t biggest = 0; uint16_t prev = 0; bool first = true; for (uint32_t t0 = millis(); millis() - t0 < 10000;) { send(0x140 + sel, d); twai_message_t m; while (twai_receive(&m, pdMS_TO_TICKS(2)) == ESP_OK) if (m.identifier == 0x140u + sel && m.data[0] == 0x9C) { const uint16_t e = (uint16_t)(m.data[6] | (m.data[7] << 8)); lo = std::min(lo, e); hi = std::max(hi, e); if (!first) { const int32_t j = abs((int32_t)e - prev); biggest = std::max(biggest, j); } prev = e; first = false; } delay(5); } const uint32_t range = hi > 32767 ? 65536 : hi > 16383 ? 32768 : 16384; Serial.printf(" encoder min %u max %u, largest jump %ld -> %u counts per turn (%s)\n", lo, hi, (long)biggest, (unsigned)range, biggest > 8192 ? "wrap seen: sure" : "no wrap seen: turn further to be sure"); Serial.println(" (the robot firmware detects this by itself; this is a cross-check)"); } static void help() { Serial.println("\nkeys: 1/2 motor ID | r on | o off | + / - torque test | e encoder test | s status + scan | h help"); } void setup() { Serial.begin(115200); delay(1500); Serial.println("\n=== CAN bench probe: ESP32-S3 TWAI + SN65HVD230 + LK motors ==="); Serial.printf("pins: CTX GPIO%d, CRX GPIO%d, 1 Mbit/s\n", PIN_CAN_TX, PIN_CAN_RX); self_test(); Serial.println("\n== 2. bus scan (normal mode) =="); if (!install(TWAI_MODE_NORMAL)) { Serial.println("TWAI install failed"); return; } scan(true); status("scan"); help(); } void loop() { static uint32_t last = 0; if (Serial.available()) { const char k = Serial.read(); if (k == '1' || k == '2') { sel = k - '0'; Serial.printf("motor %u selected\n", sel); } else if (k == 'r') { const uint8_t d[8] = {0x88}; send(0x140 + sel, d); Serial.println("on"); } else if (k == 'o') { const uint8_t d[8] = {0x80}; send(0x140 + sel, d); Serial.println("off"); } else if (k == '+') torque_test(+0.2f); else if (k == '-') torque_test(-0.2f); else if (k == 'e') encoder_test(); else if (k == 's') { scan(true); status("bus"); } else if (k == 'h') help(); } twai_status_info_t s; twai_get_status_info(&s); if (s.state == TWAI_STATE_BUS_OFF) { Serial.println("BUS OFF -> recovering (check wiring/termination)"); twai_initiate_recovery(); delay(100); twai_start(); } if (millis() - last > 2000) { last = millis(); scan(false); } }

// Minimal Arduino stand-in for compiling firmware sources on a PC (unit tests only). #pragma once #include <cstdint> #include <cstring> #include <cmath> #include <algorithm> #ifndef PI #define PI 3.14159265358979323846f #endif namespace fake { inline uint32_t us = 0; } inline uint32_t micros() { return fake::us; } inline uint32_t millis() { return fake::us / 1000; }

uint8_t data_length_code; uint8_t data[8]; } twai_message_t; typedef struct { twai_mode_t mode; int tx_io, rx_io; uint32_t tx_queue_len, rx_queue_len; } twai_general_config_t; typedef struct { int brp; } twai_timing_config_t; typedef struct { uint32_t acceptance_code, acceptance_mask; bool single_filter; } twai_filter_config_t; #define TWAI_GENERAL_CONFIG_DEFAULT(tx, rx, mode) {mode, tx, rx, 5, 5} #define TWAI_TIMING_CONFIG_1MBITS() {4} #define TWAI_FILTER_CONFIG_ACCEPT_ALL() {0, 0xFFFFFFFF, true} typedef enum { TWAI_STATE_STOPPED, TWAI_STATE_RUNNING, TWAI_STATE_BUS_OFF, TWAI_STATE_RECOVERING } twai_state_t; typedef struct { twai_state_t state; uint32_t msgs_to_tx, msgs_to_rx, tx_error_counter, rx_error_counter, tx_failed_count, rx_missed_count, rx_overrun_count, arb_lost_count, bus_error_count; } twai_status_info_t; namespace fake { inline std::vector<twai_message_t> tx; inline std::deque<twai_message_t> rx; inline bool installed = false, started = false; inline int tx_queue_free = 1000; inline twai_state_t state = TWAI_STATE_STOPPED; inline int recover_polls = 0; // status reads until a requested recovery completes inline int recoveries = 0, starts = 0; } inline esp_err_t twai_driver_install(const twai_general_config_t*, const twai_timing_config_t*, const twai_filter_config_t*) { fake::installed = true; return ESP_OK; } inline esp_err_t twai_start() { if (!fake::installed || fake::state == TWAI_STATE_BUS_OFF || fake::state == TWAI_STATE_RECOVERING) return ESP_FAIL; fake::started = true; fake::state = TWAI_STATE_RUNNING; ++fake::starts; return ESP_OK; } inline esp_err_t twai_initiate_recovery() { if (fake::state != TWAI_STATE_BUS_OFF) return ESP_FAIL; fake::state = TWAI_STATE_RECOVERING; fake::recover_polls = 2; ++fake::recoveries; return ESP_OK; } inline esp_err_t twai_get_status_info(twai_status_info_t* s) { if (fake::state == TWAI_STATE_RECOVERING && --fake::recover_polls <= 0) fake::state = TWAI_STATE_STOPPED; *s = {}; s->state = fake::state; return ESP_OK; } inline esp_err_t twai_transmit(const twai_message_t* m, uint32_t) { if (fake::state != TWAI_STATE_RUNNING || fake::tx_queue_free <= 0) return ESP_FAIL; fake::tx.push_back(*m); return ESP_OK; } inline esp_err_t twai_receive(twai_message_t* m, uint32_t) { if (fake::rx.empty()) return ESP_FAIL; *m = fake::rx.front(); fake::rx.pop_front(); return ESP_OK; }

"""Raspberry Pi side of the balancing robot: ESP32 link, LD19 lidar, mapping, navigation, camera, eyes, web app."""

"""Start everything: python3 -m robot [--config config.json]""" import argparse, json, pathlib from aiohttp import web from .brain import Brain from .camera import Camera from .server import make_app DEFAULT = { "esp32_port": "/dev/serial0", # Pi UART (GPIO14/15), enable it with raspi-config, disable the serial console "lidar": True, # V1 has the LD19 on top (False = map from the front sonar, as in V2) "lidar_port": "/dev/ttyUSB0", # LD19 kit adapter board on the micro-USB OTG port "lidar_offset_deg": 0.0, # robot-frame angle of the lidar's 0° mark: calibrate with a wall straight ahead "lidar_clockwise": True, "data_dir": "data", # map.png, map.npz, scans/*.npz "log_scans": True, "explore_speed": 0.4, "goto_speed": 0.4, "eyes": True, "camera_size": [800, 600], "camera_fps": 20, "ai_camera": True, # Raspberry Pi AI Camera: person / cat detection on the sensor "ai_model": "/usr/share/imx500-models/imx500_network_ssd_mobilenetv2_fpnlite_320x320_pp.rpk", "http_port": 8080, "voice": { # microphones + speaker + Claude (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment) "enabled": True, "wake_phrase": "hey robot|robot", # alternatives separated by | "push_to_talk_only": False, # True: only listen after the Talk button in the app "language": "en", # speech recognition / synthesis language "stt": "vosk", # "vosk" (offline) or "http" (Whisper server, e.g. on the Jetson) "vosk_model": "/home/pi/models/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15", "stt_url": "", # e.g. "http://jetson.local:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions" "tts": "piper", # "piper" or "espeak" "piper_model": "/home/pi/models/en_US-lessac-low.onnx", "claude_model": "claude-haiku-5-5", "mic_gain_db": 0.0, "mic_spacing_m": 0.124, # V1.1 front panel (V2: 0.086) "face_speaker": True, # turn toward whoever says the wake phrase "audio_device": None, # None = default ALSA card (the I2S voice card) }, } def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--config", default="config.json") a = ap.parse_args() cfg = dict(DEFAULT) p = pathlib.Path(a.config) if p.exists(): cfg.update(json.loads(p.read_text())) brain = Brain(cfg) cam = Camera(tuple(cfg["camera_size"]), cfg["camera_fps"], ai_model=cfg["ai_model"] if cfg.get("ai_camera") else None) from .vision import Vision brain.vision = Vision(cam, brain.data / "people") vcfg = dict(DEFAULT["voice"]); vcfg.update(cfg.get("voice") or {}) if vcfg.get("enabled"): from .voice import VoiceAgent brain.voice = VoiceAgent(vcfg, brain, cam) web.run_app(make_app(brain, cam), port=cfg["http_port"]) if __name__ == "__main__": main()

"""Microphones and speaker on the Pi's I2S bus. Hardware: 2 x ICS-43434 I2S MEMS microphones in the front panel, 124 mm apart (left: SEL=GND, right: SEL=3.3 V) on PCM_DIN, MAX98357A 3 W amp on PCM_DOUT, shared BCLK/LRCLK. Enable with dtoverlay=googlevoicehat-soundcard (the same mic + amp pair as the Google AIY Voice Kit). Capture is 48 kHz stereo 32-bit, processed here to 16 kHz mono for speech recognition. Voice at 2 m: normal speech is ~54 dB SPL there, the ICS-43434 hears it at about -66 dBFS with 29 dBA self-noise, so the raw signal is quiet but clean. We 1. high-pass at 100 Hz (motor rumble, handling), decimate to 16 kHz, 2. steer the two-mic beam to the talker (GCC-PHAT direction estimate) and sum: +3 dB against room noise, 3. detect speech with an adaptive energy gate, 4. normalise each utterance to -3 dBFS peak before speech recognition. The robot is half-duplex: the mics are ignored while the speaker plays (and 0.3 s after), so it never answers itself. """ import math, threading, time, queue import numpy as np FS_HW = 48000 FS = 16000 MIC_SPACING = 0.124 # m, centre to centre (V1.1 front panel; V2 was 0.086) - set "mic_spacing_m" in config C_SOUND = 343.0 # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- signal processing (pure, tested) class HighPass: """2nd-order Butterworth high-pass with state kept between blocks (scipy); falls back to DC removal.""" def __init__(self, fs=FS, fc=100.0): try: from scipy.signal import butter, lfilter, lfilter_zi self.b, self.a = butter(2, fc / (fs / 2), "highpass") self.zi = lfilter_zi(self.b, self.a) * 0.0 self._lf = lfilter except Exception: self._lf = None def __call__(self, x): x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64) if self._lf is None: return x - x.mean() y, self.zi = self._lf(self.b, self.a, x, zi=self.zi) return y def decimate3(x): """48 kHz -> 16 kHz: 31-tap windowed-sinc low-pass at 7 kHz, keep every 3rd sample.""" n = np.arange(-15, 16) h = np.sinc(2 * 7000 / FS_HW * n) * np.hamming(31); h /= h.sum() return np.convolve(x, h, mode="same")[::3] def gcc_phat(left, right, fs=FS, max_tau=MIC_SPACING / C_SOUND, interp=8): """Time difference of arrival right-vs-left (s, positive = sound reaches the LEFT mic first) by GCC-PHAT.""" n = len(left) + len(right) L, R = np.fft.rfft(left, n), np.fft.rfft(right, n) X = R * np.conj(L) f = np.fft.rfftfreq(n, 1 / fs) X[(f < 200) | (f > 4000)] = 0 # speech band only: empty bins would dominate after PHAT X /= np.abs(X) ** 0.8 + 1e-6 * (np.abs(X).max() + 1e-30) # beta-PHAT (0.8) is more robust than pure PHAT cc = np.fft.irfft(X, n * interp) m = min(int(interp * fs * max_tau), n * interp // 2) cc = np.concatenate((cc[-m:], cc[:m + 1])) return (np.argmax(np.abs(cc)) - m) / float(interp * fs) def direction_deg(tau, spacing=MIC_SPACING): """Bearing of the talker from straight ahead (deg, + = to the robot's left), from the TDOA.""" s = max(-1.0, min(1.0, tau * C_SOUND / spacing)) return math.degrees(math.asin(s)) def beam(left, right, tau, fs=FS): """Delay-and-sum toward the talker: delay the mic that hears it first by |tau| (fractional, via FFT) and average.""" n = len(left) k = np.fft.rfftfreq(n, 1 / fs) def shift(x, d): return np.fft.irfft(np.fft.rfft(x) * np.exp(-2j * np.pi * k * d), n) if tau >= 0: left = shift(left, tau) else: right = shift(right, -tau) return 0.5 * (left + right) def normalise(x, peak_dbfs=-3.0): p = np.max(np.abs(x)) + 1e-12 return x * (10 ** (peak_dbfs / 20) / p) def to_wav_bytes(x, fs=FS): import io, wave b = io.BytesIO() with wave.open(b, "wb") as w: w.setnchannels(1); w.setsampwidth(2); w.setframerate(fs) w.writeframes((np.clip(x, -1, 1) * 32767).astype("<i2").tobytes()) return b.getvalue() class SpeechGate: """Adaptive energy voice-activity detector on 20 ms frames. feed() returns a finished utterance (np array) or None. Starts when energy exceeds the noise floor by `on_db` for 3 frames, ends after `hang` s below `off_db`.""" def __init__(self, fs=FS, frame=0.02, on_db=9.0, off_db=5.0, hang=0.7, min_len=0.35, max_len=10.0, pre=0.3): self.fs, self.n = fs, int(fs * frame) self.on_db, self.off_db, self.hang, self.min_len, self.max_len = on_db, off_db, hang, min_len, max_len self.floor = None self.buf = np.zeros(0) self.pre = [np.zeros(0)] * max(1, int(pre / frame)) self.active, self.utt, self.quiet, self.loud = False, [], 0.0, 0 def reset(self): self.active, self.utt, self.quiet, self.loud = False, [], 0.0, 0 def feed(self, x): self.buf = np.concatenate((self.buf, x)) out = None while len(self.buf) >= self.n: f, self.buf = self.buf[:self.n], self.buf[self.n:] e = 10 * math.log10(np.mean(f * f) + 1e-14) if self.floor is None: self.floor = e if not self.active: self.floor += (0.05 if e > self.floor else 0.3) * (e - self.floor) # tracks noise, slowly upwards self.loud = self.loud + 1 if e > self.floor + self.on_db else 0 self.pre = self.pre[1:] + [f] if self.loud >= 3: self.active, self.utt, self.quiet = True, list(self.pre), 0.0 else: self.utt.append(f) self.quiet = self.quiet + self.n / self.fs if e < self.floor + self.off_db else 0.0 length = len(self.utt) * self.n / self.fs if self.quiet >= self.hang or length >= self.max_len: u = np.concatenate(self.utt); self.reset() if length - self.quiet >= self.min_len: out = u return out class Frontend: """(N, 2) float blocks at 48 kHz -> (mono 16 kHz beam toward the talker, bearing deg).""" def __init__(self, spacing=MIC_SPACING): self.hp = (HighPass(FS_HW), HighPass(FS_HW)) self.spacing = spacing def __call__(self, stereo48): l = decimate3(self.hp[0](stereo48[:, 0])); r = decimate3(self.hp[1](stereo48[:, 1])) tau = gcc_phat(l, r, max_tau=self.spacing / C_SOUND) return beam(l, r, tau), direction_deg(tau, self.spacing) # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- hardware class Audio: """Continuous capture + playback on the I2S sound card (sounddevice / PortAudio). Without hardware it still works as a no-op so the rest of the robot runs (and the tests can inject audio with feed()).""" def __init__(self, device=None, gain_db=0.0, on_utterance=None, spacing=MIC_SPACING): self.spacing = spacing self.on_utterance = on_utterance or (lambda u, bearing: None) self.gate = SpeechGate() self.gain = 10 ** (gain_db / 20) self.speaking_until = 0.0 self.listening = True # False = push-to-talk only and not pressed self.level_db = -120.0 self.bearing = 0.0 self._q = queue.Queue(maxsize=50) self.ok = False try: import sounddevice as sd self.sd = sd self.stream = sd.InputStream(device=device, samplerate=FS_HW, channels=2, dtype="float32", blocksize=4800, callback=lambda d, *_: self._q.put_nowait(d.copy()) if not self._q.full() else None) self.stream.start(); self.ok = True except Exception as e: print("audio input unavailable:", e); self.sd = None threading.Thread(target=self._run, daemon=True).start() def feed(self, stereo48): self._q.put(np.asarray(stereo48, dtype=np.float64)) def _run(self): bearings = [] fe = Frontend(self.spacing) while True: d = self._q.get() mono, b = fe(d * self.gain) self.level_db = 20 * math.log10(np.sqrt(np.mean(mono * mono)) + 1e-12) if time.time() < self.speaking_until or not self.listening: self.gate.reset(); continue if self.gate.active: bearings.append(b) u = self.gate.feed(mono) if u is not None: self.bearing = float(np.median(bearings)) if bearings else b bearings = [] self.on_utterance(normalise(u), self.bearing) def play(self, x, fs): """Play mono float audio (blocking). Mutes the microphones meanwhile.""" x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float32) dur = len(x) / fs self.speaking_until = time.time() + dur + 0.3 if self.sd is None: time.sleep(min(dur, 0.05)); return if fs != FS_HW: # simple linear resample to the card rate t = np.arange(int(len(x) * FS_HW / fs)) * fs / FS_HW x = np.interp(t, np.arange(len(x)), x).astype(np.float32) self.sd.play(x, FS_HW, blocking=True) self.speaking_until = time.time() + 0.3

"""The Pi-side robot: ties together the ESP32 link, lidar (optional: V2 has none and maps with the sonar), mapping, obstacle avoidance, exploration and the eyes. Runs a 20 Hz decision loop in a thread; the web server (server.py) only sets intents and reads state.""" import math, re, threading, time, pathlib import numpy as np from .link import Link, MODE_VELOCITY, MODE_TURN_BY, MODE_TURN_TO, MODE_FLIP, MODE_DOCK, MODE_UNDOCK from . import dock as dockmod from .ld19 import LD19, level_scan from .mapper import Mapper from .navigation import Avoider, FrontierExplorer, Planner, PathFollower LEVEL_MAX = 0.09 # rad: only add scans to the map while the body (and the lidar plane) tilts less than ~5° SONAR_LEVEL_MAX = 0.06 # rad: same for sonar readings (V2) class Brain: def __init__(self, cfg): self.cfg = cfg self.data = pathlib.Path(cfg.get("data_dir", "data")); self.data.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) self.events = [] self.link = Link(cfg.get("esp32_port", "/dev/serial0"), on_event=self._event) self.lidar = None if cfg.get("lidar", True): self.lidar = LD19(cfg.get("lidar_port", "/dev/ttyUSB0"), offset_deg=cfg.get("lidar_offset_deg", 0.0), clockwise=cfg.get("lidar_clockwise", True)) self.mapper = self._new_mapper() self.avoider, self.explorer = Avoider(), FrontierExplorer(speed=cfg.get("explore_speed", 0.4)) self.planner, self.follower = Planner(), PathFollower(speed=cfg.get("goto_speed", 0.4)) self.eyes = None if cfg.get("eyes", True): from .eyes import Eyes self.eyes = Eyes() from .headlight import Headlight self.headlight = Headlight(cfg.get("headlight_pwmchip", "/sys/class/pwm/pwmchip0")) # intents (set by the web app) self.mode = "manual" # manual | explore | goto | turn self.joy = (0.0, 0.0); self.joy_t = 0.0 self.arm_req = self.disarm_req = False self.auto_standup, self.avoid_on = True, True self.turn_angle, self.turn_t0 = 0.0, 0.0 self.goto_xy = None self.agent_cmd, self.agent_until, self.flip_t0 = (0.0, 0.0), 0.0, 0.0 self.voice = None # VoiceAgent, attached by __main__ when voice is enabled self.vision = None # Vision (AI Camera detections + face ID), attached by __main__ self.tracker = None # follow mode: the person being followed self.cmd = (0.0, 0.0) self.dock_pose = dockmod.load_dock(self.data / "dock.json") # map pose of the robot when docked self.pilot, self.dock_t0, self.dock_out = None, 0.0, (MODE_VELOCITY, 0.0, 0.0) self._auto_dock_t = 0.0 self._docked_t = None # when the last docking finished (re-dock if the contacts open soon after) self.scan_pts = np.zeros((0, 2)) self._last_scan_t = 0.0 self._last_save = time.time() threading.Thread(target=self._loop, daemon=True).start() def _event(self, txt): self.events = (self.events + [time.strftime("%H:%M:%S ") + txt])[-30:] print("[esp32]", txt) # ---------------- intents ---------------- def joystick(self, v, w): self.joy, self.joy_t = (float(v), float(w)), time.time() if abs(v) > 0.02 or abs(w) > 0.05: self.mode = "manual" def command(self, name, **kw): if name == "arm": self.arm_req = True elif name == "disarm": self.disarm_req = True; self.mode = "manual" elif name == "stop": self.mode = "manual"; self.joy = (0.0, 0.0) elif name == "explore": self.mode = "explore"; self.explorer = FrontierExplorer(speed=self.cfg.get("explore_speed", 0.4)) elif name == "turn": self.mode, self.turn_angle, self.turn_t0 = "turn", math.radians(float(kw.get("angle", 90))), time.time(); self.link.seq += 1 elif name == "flip": self.mode, self.flip_t0 = "flip", time.time(); self.link.seq += 1 elif name == "goto": self.goto_xy = (float(kw["x"]), float(kw["y"])) path = self.planner.search(self.mapper.grid, self.mapper.pose[:2], goal_xy=self.goto_xy) if path: self.follower.path, self.mode = path, "goto" else: self._event("no path to that point (unknown or blocked)") elif name == "auto_standup": self.auto_standup = bool(kw.get("on", True)) elif name == "avoid": self.avoid_on = bool(kw.get("on", True)) elif name == "light": on = bool(kw.get("on", False)) self.headlight.set(float(kw.get("level", 1.0)) if on else 0.0) # the COB discs if self.eyes: self.eyes.light = on # and the eyes' white night light elif name == "follow": from .vision import Tracker self.tracker, self.mode = Tracker(name=kw.get("name") or None), "follow" elif name == "dock": self._start_dock() elif name == "undock": self._docked_t = None self.mode, self.dock_t0 = "undock", time.time(); self._event("charge contacts opened: docking again"); self._start_dock() # flat battery: the ESP32 cuts the power in 20 s -> halt the Pi cleanly first (SD card safety) if fresh and tel.power_off_pending and not getattr(self, "_halting", False): self._halting = True; """Raspberry Pi AI Camera (or Camera Module 3) -> MJPEG stream, encoded on the Pi's hardware JPEG/ISP path (Picamera2). MJPEG works in every browser with a plain <img> tag and costs little CPU. For lower bandwidth use WebRTC via mediamtx (see README: 'Lower-latency video'), which needs no change here. """ import io, threading, time class StreamingOutput(io.BufferedIOBase): def __init__(self): self.frame = None self.cond = threading.Condition() self.count = 0 def write(self, buf): with self.cond: self.frame = bytes(buf); self.count += 1 self.cond.notify_all() return len(buf) def wait(self, last_count, timeout=1.0): with self.cond: self.cond.wait_for(lambda: self.count != last_count, timeout) return self.frame, self.count class Camera: def __init__(self, size=(800, 600), fps=20, quality=70, ai_model=None): self.output = StreamingOutput() self.ok = False self.imx500 = None try: from picamera2 import Picamera2 from picamera2.encoders import MJPEGEncoder, Quality from picamera2.outputs import FileOutput num = None if ai_model: # AI Camera: load the network onto the IMX500 before opening the camera try: from picamera2.devices import IMX500 self.imx500 = IMX500(ai_model); num = self.imx500.camera_num except Exception as e: print("AI camera network not loaded:", e) self.cam = Picamera2(num) if num is not None else Picamera2() cfg = self.cam.create_video_configuration(main={"size": size, "format": "RGB888"}, controls={"FrameRate": fps}, buffer_count=6) self.cam.configure(cfg) q = Quality.MEDIUM if quality < 80 else Quality.HIGH self.cam.start_recording(MJPEGEncoder(), FileOutput(self.output), quality=q) try: # continuous autofocus on the Camera Module 3 (the AI Camera has manual focus: no-op) from libcamera import controls self.cam.set_controls({"AfMode": controls.AfModeEnum.Continuous}) except Exception: pass self.ok = True except Exception as e: # no camera (e.g. on a laptop): serve a placeholder print("camera unavailable:", e) threading.Thread(target=self._placeholder, daemon=True).start() def _placeholder(self): try: from PIL import Image, ImageDraw except ImportError: return while True: im = Image.new("RGB", (640, 480), (40, 44, 52)); d = ImageDraw.Draw(im) d.text((20, 220), time.strftime("no camera %H:%M:%S"), fill=(220, 220, 220)) b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG"); self.output.write(b.getvalue()) time.sleep(0.5) def close(self): if self.ok: self.cam.stop_recording()

"""Autonomous docking onto the vertical charger. The dock is a column (80 mm wide at lidar height) standing on a floor plate. The robot parks 0.45 m in front of it, facing away, then reverses slowly. Each lidar scan: find the column's flat face behind the robot, fit a line -> the robot's pose in the dock frame (distance X out from the face, lateral offset Y, heading error psi). Steer so Y and psi go to zero; at the lean distance tell the ESP32 to lean back (CMD_DOCK with a new seq). The ESP32 lands the plate on the dock face; the rods touch the contacts -> CHARGING. No contact -> it stands up again: drive out and retry (3 tries). The first successful dock saves the dock's map pose (data/dock.json), so 'dock' later can plan to the approach point from anywhere on the map. Geometry (case/body_case.py): column front plane at lidar height is 74 mm behind the lidar when docked; upright the plate touches the dock face 14 mm before that (X = 60 mm) and the rods are in the funnels from X = 68 mm. The robot cannot slide sideways, so the lidar guidance has to bring it in within ~±5 mm (sim: it does); the funnels take the rest by turning it slightly, the wings only stop a bad approach from hitting the rods. """ import json, math, pathlib from dataclasses import dataclass import numpy as np COL_HALF_W = 0.040 # m, column half width (DOCK_TOWER) X_DOCKED = 0.074 # m, lidar -> column face when docked X_LEAN = 0.093 # m: lean back from here: the axle is on the floor ridge's crest (sim: leaning from behind it # meant rolling down into the dock uncontrolled) X_APPROACH = 0.45 # m: the line-up point on the dock axis, where the straight reverse starts SEARCH_R = 1.2 # m: look for the column this close behind the robot V_FAR, V_NEAR = -0.07, -0.04 # m/s K_Y, K_PSI = 6.0, 2.2 # psi_des = K_Y * Y (rad per m), yaw rate = K_PSI * (psi_des - psi) PSI_MAX = math.radians(20) MAX_TRIES = 3 LINEUP_MAX = 35.0 # s: a line-up that hasn't converged by then counts as a failed try LIDAR_H = 0.177 # m, lidar above the axle: leaning by p moves it 0.177·sin(p) along the dock axis @dataclass class DockFix: X: float # m, lidar -> column face, along the face normal Y: float # m, robot lateral offset in the dock frame (+ = robot is to the dock's left) psi: float # rad, robot heading relative to the dock axis (0 = facing straight away from it) n: int # points on the face rms: float # m, line fit residual tape: bool = False # found by its retro-reflective strips (an ID: nothing else in the room looks like it) def _fit_line(p): c = p.mean(axis=0) u, s, vt = np.linalg.svd(p - c, full_matrices=False) d = vt[0] # direction along the face n = np.array([-d[1], d[0]]) # normal res = (p - c) @ n return c, d, n, res TAPE_W, TAPE_PITCH = 0.025, 0.049 # m: the two retro-reflective strips on the column face, centre to centre TAPE_MIN = 200 # LD19 intensity of the tape (paint/walls read ~60-160 close up; calibrate: config) def _pose_from_face(c, cen_t): """Robot pose in the dock frame from the face points c (robot frame) and the face centre cen_t.""" cen, d, n, res = _fit_line(c) if n @ cen > 0: n = -n # normal from the face towards the robot (lidar at 0) t = np.array([-n[1], n[0]]) rr = -cen_t return float(rr @ n), float(rr @ t), float(math.atan2(-n[1], n[0])), float(np.sqrt(np.mean(res ** 2))) def fit_dock_tape(angles, ranges, intensity, behind=True, tape_min=TAPE_MIN, max_r=SEARCH_R): """The dock by its tape: two bright strips 49 mm apart (centre to centre), 25 mm wide, in line. Their midpoint is the face centre (no edge guessing); the column face around them gives the angle. behind=False: look all round.""" a = np.asarray(angles, float); r = np.asarray(ranges, float); it = np.asarray(intensity, float) ok = (r > 0.02) & (r < max_r) P = np.c_[r * np.cos(a), r * np.sin(a)] if behind: ok &= P[:, 0] < -0.02 bright = ok & (it >= tape_min) idx = np.where(bright)[0] if len(idx) < 2: return None # strips = runs of bright points (split where neighbours are > 15 mm apart), in angle order o = idx[np.argsort(np.mod(a[idx], 2 * np.pi))] runs, cur = [], [o[0]] for i0, i1 in zip(o[:-1], o[1:]): if np.hypot(*(P[i1] - P[i0])) > 0.015: runs.append(cur); cur = [] cur.append(i1) runs.append(cur) strips = [] for rn in runs: q = P[rn] w = np.hypot(*(q[-1] - q[0])) if len(q) > 1 else 0.0 if w < 0.045: strips.append((q.mean(axis=0), w, len(q))) # one strip (or part of it, at a grazing angle) best = None for i in range(len(strips)): for j in range(i + 1, len(strips)): ci, cj = strips[i][0], strips[j][0] dd = np.hypot(*(ci - cj)) if abs(dd - TAPE_PITCH) < 0.012 and abs(np.hypot(*ci) - np.hypot(*cj)) < 0.05: m = 0.5 * (ci + cj); dist = np.hypot(*m) if best is None or dist < best[0]: best = (dist, m) if best is None: return None m = best[1] face = P[ok & (np.hypot(P[:, 0] - m[0], P[:, 1] - m[1]) < 0.042)] # the 80 mm face, not its sides if len(face) < 3: return None for thr in (0.008, 0.005): cen, d, n, res = _fit_line(face) keep = np.abs(res) < thr if keep.sum() < 3: break face = face[keep] X, Y, psi, rms = _pose_from_face(face, m) return DockFix(X=X, Y=Y, psi=psi, n=int(len(face)), rms=rms, tape=True) def fit_dock(angles, ranges, prev: "DockFix" = None, intensity=None, require_tape=False): """Find the dock column behind the robot in one scan (robot frame, x forward, y left; angle 0 = forward).
