import cadquery as cq, os, glob import robot_paths as RP from OCP.BRepTools import BRepTools from OCP.BRep import BRep_Builder from OCP.TopoDS import TopoDS_Shape D = str(RP.models_dir()) def load(name): """STEP -> cq.Shape, cached as BREP (loading the camera STEP takes ~1 min).""" br = os.path.join(D, name.rsplit(".", 1)[0] + ".brep") if os.path.exists(br): s = TopoDS_Shape(); BRepTools.Read_s(s, br, BRep_Builder()); return cq.Shape.cast(s) sh = cq.importers.importStep(os.path.join(D, name)) s = cq.Compound.makeCompound([v for v in sh.vals()]) if len(sh.vals()) > 1 else sh.val() BRepTools.Write_s(s.wrapped, br) return s

"""List body surfaces that face the print bed (build direction = -X, bed at x = X_IN_F) and are not on the bed. Faces steeper than 45 deg from vertical, i.e. normal_x > cos(45), would need support (small bridges are OK).""" import sys, importlib, math import robot_paths as RP; RP.add_sources() import cadquery as cq from OCP.BRepGProp import BRepGProp_Face from OCP.gp import gp_Pnt, gp_Vec mod = importlib.import_module(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'body_case') body = mod.build_body().val() bed = mod.X_IN_F rows = [] for f in body.Faces(): u0, u1, v0, v1 = f._uvBounds() prop = BRepGProp_Face(f.wrapped); p = gp_Pnt(); n = gp_Vec() prop.Normal((u0 + u1) / 2, (v0 + v1) / 2, p, n) n.Normalize() if n.Magnitude() > 1e-9 else None if n.X() > math.cos(math.radians(45)) + 1e-3: bb = f.BoundingBox() if abs(bb.xmin - bed) < 0.05 and abs(bb.xmax - bed) < 0.05: continue # on the bed span = min(bb.ylen, bb.zlen) # bridge length ~ the shorter side rows.append((f.Area(), span, round(bb.xmin, 1), round(bb.ymin, 1), round(bb.ymax, 1), round(bb.zmin, 1), round(bb.zmax, 1))) rows.sort(reverse=True) big = [r for r in rows if r[0] > 15] print(f"{len(rows)} downward faces off the bed; {len(big)} larger than 15 mm2:") for r in big[:25]: print(f" area {r[0]:7.1f} mm2 span {r[1]:5.1f} x={r[2]} y {r[3]}..{r[4]} z {r[5]}..{r[6]}")

"""Perfboard layout on the 2.54 mm hole grid (component side faces +x, towards the front). Board: standard 5 x 7 cm double-sided FR4, 24 x 18 holes, 70 (robot y) x 50 (robot z), back face at x = X_BACK + BOARD_STANDOFF, centre bc.PB_CENTER. Hole (k, j): y = Y0 + 2.54 k, z = Z0 + 2.54 j (k 0..23, j 0..17). Regions: the ESP32 DevKit sits on two 22-pin female header rows (j 8 and j 17) over y -60..-4; under it there is 8.5 mm of height for flat parts (74AHCT125, resistors). The CAN board stands on spacers at y -64..-31, z 81-91. Plugs go in the free area below the DevKit (y -31..+6, z 77..98). """ import body_case as bc XB = bc.X_BACK + bc.BOARD_STANDOFF # board back face XF = XB + 1.6 # component face CY, CZ = bc.PB_CENTER NK, NJ = 24, 18 # standard 5 x 7 cm board: 24 x 18 holes (432), 2.54 mm, centred Y0 = CY - (NK - 1) * 2.54 / 2 # hole k = 0 at the -Y end (5.8 mm from the edge) Z0 = CZ - (NJ - 1) * 2.54 / 2 # hole j = 0 at the bottom (3.4 mm from the edge) DK_COLS, DK_ROWS = (1, 22), (8, 17) # DevKit female headers: holes k 1-22 on rows j 8 and 17 def hole(k, j): assert 0 <= k < NK and 0 <= j < NJ, (k, j) return (Y0 + 2.54 * k, Z0 + 2.54 * j) # plugs: name -> (k of pin 1, j, pins, pitch in holes, height, kind). Rows j 0 and 3 stay at k >= 12, clear of the # CAN board standing on spacers over k 0-11 (y -64..-31, z 81-91). PLUGS = { "J2": (12, 0, 4, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), # The zone array is fitted INSTEAD of the sonar, so it takes the sonar's place on the board with # a 6-pin housing: k 12..17 is exactly six holes before J1 at k 18. Only one of J2 / J2T is # populated on a given robot. "J2T": (12, 0, 6, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), "J1": (18, 0, 2, 2, 8.0, "XT30PW right-angle PCB plug (15 A)"), "J7": (12, 3, 3, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), "J5": (17, 3, 5, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), "J3": (1, 6, 4, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), "J4": (6, 6, 3, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), "J6": (10, 6, 5, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), "J8": (16, 6, 6, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), # IR receivers: 3V3, GND, GPIO13-16 "J9": (22, 6, 1, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), # power switch OFF: GPIO21 (100 k pull-down on the board) } def plug_pin(name, i): k, j, n, p, h, _ = PLUGS[name] y, z = hole(k + i * p, j) return (XF + h, y, z) # wire end = top of the housing def plug_box(name): k, j, n, p, h, kind = PLUGS[name] y1, z = hole(k, j); y2, _ = hole(k + (n - 1) * p, j) if kind.startswith("XT30"): return (XF, XF + h, (y1 + y2) / 2 - 5.1, (y1 + y2) / 2 + 5.1, z - 2.6, z + 2.6) return (XF, XF + h, y1 - 1.27, y2 + 1.27, z - 2.5, z + 2.5) # flat parts: name -> (k1, j1, k2, j2, height, what). Resistors 1/4 W lying flat, leads 10.16 mm apart (4 holes); # all of them and the 74AHCT125 sit under the DevKit (rows 9-16 are free between its header rows, 8.5 mm of height). PARTS = { "U1 74AHCT125 (DIP-14)": (8, 11, 14, 14, 4.5, "Pi MOSI -> 5 V WS2812 data; 1OE to GND, unused inputs to GND"), "R4 100k (VBAT top)": (1, 10, 5, 10, 2.5, "J7-1 -> GPIO1"), "R5 12k (VBAT bottom)": (1, 11, 5, 11, 2.5, "GPIO1 -> GND"), "R6 100k (dock top)": (1, 12, 5, 12, 2.5, "J7-2 -> GPIO6"), "R7 12k (dock bottom)": (1, 13, 5, 13, 2.5, "GPIO6 -> GND"), "R8 56k (USB top)": (1, 14, 5, 14, 2.5, "J7-3 -> GPIO7"), "R9 10k (USB bottom)": (1, 15, 5, 15, 2.5, "GPIO7 -> GND"), "R2 1k (echo top)": (16, 10, 20, 10, 2.5, "J2-3 -> GPIO11"), "R3 2k (echo bottom)": (16, 11, 20, 11, 2.5, "GPIO11 -> GND"), "R1 330 (eye data)": (16, 12, 20, 12, 2.5, "U1 1Y -> J4-2"), "R10 330 (LED R)": (16, 13, 20, 13, 2.5, "GPIO38 -> J6-2"), "R11 330 (LED G)": (16, 14, 20, 14, 2.5, "GPIO39 -> J6-3"), "R12 330 (LED B)": (16, 15, 20, 15, 2.5, "GPIO40 -> J6-4"), "C1 470 uF 10 V (6.3 x 11)": (22, 0, 23, 0, 11.0, "5 V bus, beside the 5 V input plug J1 (was under J8)"), } def part_box(name): k1, j1, k2, j2, h, _ = PARTS[name] y1, z1 = hole(k1, j1); y2, z2 = hole(k2, j2) if name.startswith("C1"): c = ((y1 + y2) / 2, z1) return (XF, XF + h, c[0] - 3.2, c[0] + 3.2, c[1] - 3.2, c[1] + 3.2) return (XF, XF + h, min(y1, y2) - 1.2, max(y1, y2) + 1.2, min(z1, z2) - 1.2, max(z1, z2) + 1.2)

"""Where everything lives on this machine. The CAD and electrical scripts were written on the Claude VM, whose layout is /home/claude/case the case sources (this directory) /home/claude/wheel_adapter the wheel-adapter sources /home/claude/robot the git repository /home/claude/models/bought bought-part STEP models /home/claude/mf_step the MF6015 motor STEP In a git checkout the same files are cad_src/case, cad_src/wheel_adapter and the repository root itself. Nothing below is hard-coded to either layout: the source trees are found from this file's own location (it ships next to the case sources, so it is in the right place on both machines), the repository by walking up to the directory that holds firmware/ and sim/, and the VM paths remain as a last-resort fallback. So the same code runs unchanged on the VM and on a developer machine. Every root can be overridden by an environment variable: ROBOT_CASE ROBOT_WHEEL_ADAPTER ROBOT_ROOT ROBOT_OUT ROBOT_MODELS ROBOT_MF6015_STEP BOT_WS is also honoured, for the workspace layout tools/make_workspace.sh builds (case/, wheel_adapter/, robot/, v2site/, bom/, models/, mf_step/ side by side, all symlinked back into this repo). Each of its directories is used only if it exists, so a partial workspace falls back to the layout found from this file. From a script in this directory: import robot_paths as RP From anywhere else in the repo: import sys, pathlib sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve() .parents[1] / "cad_src" / "case")) import robot_paths as RP """ import os import pathlib import sys Path = pathlib.Path _VM = Path("/home/claude") # the Claude VM layout, used only if it is really there def _env(name): v = os.environ.get(name) return Path(v).expanduser() if v else None _WS = _env("BOT_WS") # workspace built by tools/make_workspace.sh, if any def _ws(*parts): """A directory inside the BOT_WS workspace, but only if it is really there.""" if _WS is None: return None p = _WS.joinpath(*parts) return p if p.is_dir() else None # ---------------------------------------------------------------- source trees # This file sits in the case source directory, so its own parent is the answer on # both machines: /home/claude/case on the VM, <repo>/cad_src/case in a checkout. CASE = _env("ROBOT_CASE") or _ws("case") or Path(__file__).resolve().parent # ... and the wheel adapter is its sibling in both layouts. WHEEL_ADAPTER = _env("ROBOT_WHEEL_ADAPTER") or _ws("wheel_adapter") or CASE.parent / "wheel_adapter" def _find_repo(): p = _env("ROBOT_ROOT") or _ws("robot") if p: return p for d in [CASE, *CASE.parents]: # a checkout: walk up to the root if (d / "firmware" / "esp32").is_dir() and (d / "sim").is_dir(): return d if (_VM / "robot" / "sim").is_dir(): # the VM: the repo is a sibling return _VM / "robot" raise RuntimeError( "cannot find the repository root (no parent of %s holds both firmware/ and sim/, " "and %s does not exist). Set ROBOT_ROOT to the checkout." % (CASE, _VM / "robot")) REPO = _find_repo() SIM = REPO / "sim" SITE = _ws("v2site") or REPO / "site" # the published pages and their builders BOM = _ws("bom") or REPO / "bom" FIRMWARE_CONFIG = REPO / "firmware" / "esp32" / "include" / "config.h" PI_INSTALL = REPO / "pi" / "install.sh" def add_sources(): """Put the case and wheel-adapter sources on sys.path (body_case, wiring, wheel_adapter...).""" for d in (WHEEL_ADAPTER, CASE): s = str(d) if s not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, s) def source(name): """A case source file read as text (the scripts that exec parts of each other).""" return CASE / name # ---------------------------------------------------------- generated artifacts # Where assemble.py and the exporters write. On the VM this is /home/claude/case, # exactly where they have always written; in a checkout it is cad_src/case, which # .gitignore keeps out of git. Set ROBOT_OUT to collect them somewhere else. OUT = _env("ROBOT_OUT") or CASE ASSEMBLY = OUT / "assembly" # Artifacts that one script writes and another reads, with the command that makes each. MAKES = { "wiring_data.json": "python cad_src/case/dump_wiring.py", "wiring_diagram.json": "python cad_src/case/dump_wiring.py", "viewer_parts_v11.json": "python cad_src/case/export_viewer_data.py", "print_parts_v11.json": "python cad_src/case/export_print_data.py", "real_fit_report.json": "python cad_src/case/real_assembly.py", "wire_report.json": "python cad_src/case/wire_check.py", } def out(name): """Where to write a generated artifact (creating the directory if needed).""" OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) return OUT / name def artifact(name): """Where to read a generated artifact: the first copy that exists.""" tried = [] for d in dict.fromkeys((OUT, CASE, _VM / "case", REPO / "elec")): # dedup, keep order p = d / name tried.append(str(p)) if p.exists(): return p how = MAKES.get(name) raise FileNotFoundError( "%s not found. Looked in:\n %s\n%s" % ( name, "\n ".join(tried), ("Generate it with: %s (needs cadquery)" % how) if how else "")) # ------------------------------------------------------------- bought-part CAD def models_dir(): """Directory of bought-part STEP models (models/fetch_models.sh downloads them).""" p = _env("ROBOT_MODELS") if p: return p for d in (_ws("models", "bought"), REPO / "models" / "bought", _VM / "models" / "bought"): if d and d.is_dir(): return d return REPO / "models" / "bought" def mf6015_step(): """The MF6015 motor STEP. #!/usr/bin/env bash # Regenerate the CAD and electrical artifacts, in dependency order. # # cad_src/rebuild.sh # the lot # cad_src/rebuild.sh --fast # skip the two viewer exports (the slow, multi-MB ones) # # Needs CadQuery (ml/setup_mac.sh --cad) and the bought-part models (models/fetch_models.sh), # plus models/bought/mf6015.step, which is not redistributable: download it from the LKMTECH # or dealer product page. Everything is written where robot_paths.py says (ROBOT_OUT). # # Order matters: assemble.py builds the printed parts the fit check and the exporters reuse, # and dump_wiring.py produces the wiring_data.json that elec/can_ground_check.py reads. set -euo pipefail cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." PY="$PWD/.venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$PY" ] || PY="$(command -v python3)" FAST=0 for a in "$@"; do case "$a" in --fast) FAST=1 ;; *) echo "unknown option: $a (try --fast)" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac done # ---- preflight: fail here with something actionable, not 10 minutes in ------------------- "$PY" -c "import cadquery" 2>/dev/null || { echo "CadQuery is not installed. Run: ml/setup_mac.sh --cad (or: pip install cadquery)" >&2; exit 1; } if ! ls models/bought/*.step >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "== bought-part models missing, downloading" models/fetch_models.sh fi "$PY" - <<'PREFLIGHT' || exit 1 import sys sys.path.insert(0, "cad_src/case") import robot_paths as RP try: RP.mf6015_step() except FileNotFoundError as e: sys.exit(str(e)) # the message already says where to put it PREFLIGHT step() { printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; } cd cad_src/case step "wiring harnesses -> wiring_data.json, wiring_diagram.json" "$PY" dump_wiring.py step "assembly: printed parts, meshes and masses for sim/" "$PY" assemble.py step "fit check against the real bought-part models" "$PY" real_assembly.py step "harness and connector collision check" "$PY" wire_check.py step "printed parts in print orientation -> print_parts_v11.json" "$PY" export_print_data.py if [ "$FAST" = 0 ]; then step "viewer data (placeholder components)" "$PY" export_viewer_data.py step "viewer data (real models + wiring)" "$PY" export_viewer_real.py fi cd ../.. step "electrical rules check against the regenerated wiring" (cd elec && "$PY" erc.py | tail -3 && "$PY" can_ground_check.py | tail -3) printf '\nDone. assemble.py also refreshed sim/meshes/ and sim/cad_mass.json:\n' printf ' check them in, then run sim/rebuild.sh so the MuJoCo models follow the CAD.\n'

"""Parametric MF6015 motor-mount wall section (CadQuery). The motor's fixed back face bolts to this wall: 4 x M2.5 on a 20 x 20 mm square (8 mm deep threads in the motor). A shallow pocket centers the Ø49 back section. A slot over the connector notch lets the plugs go in radially and the cables pass through into the body. Use it either as a standalone plate (4 corner M3 holes -> heat-set inserts in the chassis) or as a reference: import the STEP into your chassis CAD and boolean it into the side wall. Coordinates match the LKMTECH STEP: motor axis = X, back face at x = 29, connector notch toward +Z. Run: python3 motor_mount.py """ import cadquery as cq import pathlib BACK_FACE_X = 29.0 # motor back face in the STEP's frame BOSS_D = 49.0 # back section, Ø49 -0.05 POCKET_D = 49.4 # tune 49.2-49.6 for a snug, centered fit POCKET_DEPTH = 2.0 WALL_T = 7.0 # total wall thickness -> 5 mm under the screw heads PLATE_W = 76.0 # square plate size (standalone version) CORNER_R = 6.0 M25_CLEAR = 2.9 M25_HEAD_CB = 5.0 # counterbore Ø for M2.5 socket head (4.5 mm head) M25_CB_DEPTH = 0.0 # 0 = heads sit on the inner face; >0 to sink them SQUARE = 20.0 # motor bolt square SLOT_W = 22.0 # connector notch is ~17.4 wide; plugs need a bit more SLOT_Z0 = 12.0 # slot starts this far above the axis (connector base) SLOT_Z1 = 30.0 M3_CLEAR = 3.4 # corner holes to bolt the plate to the chassis M3_INSET = 7.0 def build(): x_out = BACK_FACE_X - POCKET_DEPTH # face toward the motor # plate: sketch in YZ, extrude +X (away from the motor) wp = cq.Workplane("YZ", origin=(x_out, 0, 0)) plate = wp.rect(PLATE_W, PLATE_W).extrude(WALL_T).edges("|X").fillet(CORNER_R) # centering pocket plate = plate.cut(cq.Workplane("YZ", origin=(x_out, 0, 0)).circle(POCKET_D / 2).extrude(POCKET_DEPTH)) # connector slot through the wall zc = (SLOT_Z0 + SLOT_Z1) / 2 plate = plate.cut(cq.Workplane("YZ", origin=(x_out - 1, 0, 0)).center(0, zc) .rect(SLOT_W, SLOT_Z1 - SLOT_Z0).extrude(WALL_T + 2) .edges("|X").fillet(2.0)) # motor screws (inserted from inside the body) h = SQUARE / 2 pts = [(-h, -h), (h, -h), (h, h), (-h, h)] plate = plate.cut(cq.Workplane("YZ", origin=(x_out - 1, 0, 0)).pushPoints(pts) .circle(M25_CLEAR / 2).extrude(WALL_T + 2)) if M25_CB_DEPTH > 0: plate = plate.cut(cq.Workplane("YZ", origin=(x_out + WALL_T - M25_CB_DEPTH, 0, 0)) .pushPoints(pts).circle(M25_HEAD_CB / 2).extrude(M25_CB_DEPTH + 1)) # chassis mounting holes c = PLATE_W / 2 - M3_INSET plate = plate.cut(cq.Workplane("YZ", origin=(x_out - 1, 0, 0)) .pushPoints([(-c, -c), (c, -c), (c, c), (-c, c)]) .circle(M3_CLEAR / 2).extrude(WALL_T + 2)) return plate if __name__ == "__main__": out = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent part = build() cq.exporters.export(part, str(out / "mf6015_motor_mount.step")) cq.exporters.export(part, str(out / "mf6015_motor_mount.stl"), tolerance=0.02, angularTolerance=0.1) under_head = WALL_T - POCKET_DEPTH - M25_CB_DEPTH print("plate %.0f x %.0f x %.0f mm, ~%.0f g PETG; material under M2.5 heads %.1f mm " "-> M2.5 x %d screws (thread engagement %.1f of 8 mm)" % (PLATE_W, PLATE_W, WALL_T, part.val().Volume() / 1000 * 1.27, under_head, int(under_head + 5), 5.0))

"""Parametric MF6015 -> 12 mm hex RC wheel adapter (CadQuery). Print orientation: hex end DOWN on the bed. The 45-degree cone under the flange means no supports are needed, and the motor-facing flange and centering spigot come out as clean top surfaces. Run: python3 wheel_adapter.py -> writes STEP + STL next to this script. """ import cadquery as cq import math, pathlib # ---------------- motor interface (from LKMTECH MF6015 v2 drawing + STEP) ------ BORE_D = 12.7 # motor centering bore, H7 (1/2") SPIGOT_D = 12.6 # printed spigot: tune 12.55-12.70 for a snug slide fit SPIGOT_L = 4.0 # bore is ~17 mm deep, 4 mm is plenty for centering PCD = 25.0 # 4 x M3 bolt circle M3_CLEAR = 3.4 M3_HEAD_CB = 6.0 # counterbore for M3 socket head (5.5 mm head) # ---------------- adapter body ------------------------------------------------- FLANGE_D = 36.0 FLANGE_T = 5.5 # plate under screw heads. M3x8 -> 2.5 mm into motor NECK_D = 18.0 NECK_L = 6.0 # standoff so the wheel clears the motor - set per wheel HEX_AF = 11.95 # 12 mm hex across flats, minus a print tolerance HEX_L = 7.0 # match the depth of your wheel's hex pocket (it must bottom out) M4_INSERT_D = 5.6 # hole for M4 heat-set insert (check your insert's spec) M4_INSERT_L = 9.0 CHAMFER = 0.6 BRIDGE_LAYER = 0.2 # layer height used by the two-layer bridge at the screw-head seats CONE_H = (FLANGE_D - NECK_D) / 2 # 45 degrees -> support-free def build(): # z = 0 is the motor mating face; +z goes into the motor, -z toward the wheel. spigot = (cq.Workplane("XY").circle(SPIGOT_D / 2).extrude(SPIGOT_L) .faces(">Z").edges().chamfer(0.8)) flange = cq.Workplane("XY").circle(FLANGE_D / 2).extrude(-FLANGE_T) cone = (cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=-FLANGE_T) .circle(FLANGE_D / 2).workplane(offset=-CONE_H) .circle(NECK_D / 2).loft()) z0 = -FLANGE_T - CONE_H neck = cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=z0).circle(NECK_D / 2).extrude(-NECK_L) z1 = z0 - NECK_L hexp = (cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=z1) .polygon(6, HEX_AF / math.cos(math.radians(30))).extrude(-HEX_L) .faces("<Z").edges().chamfer(CHAMFER)) body = spigot.union(flange).union(cone).union(neck).union(hexp) zb = z1 - HEX_L # M4 heat-set insert from the hex end, with a 45 deg pointed end (prints without a bridge, hex-down) body = body.cut(cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=zb) .circle(M4_INSERT_D / 2).extrude(M4_INSERT_L)) body = body.cut(cq.Solid.makeCone(M4_INSERT_D / 2, 0.01, M4_INSERT_D / 2, cq.Vector(0, 0, zb + M4_INSERT_L), cq.Vector(0, 0, 1))) # 4 x M3 clearance holes + counterbores opening on the wheel side. The head seat is printed with the # two-layer bridge trick (hex-down): layer 1 leaves a slot as wide as the hole, layer 2 a square, then the round # hole: clean bridges, no sacrificial membrane to drill out, no support. pts_a = [(a, PCD / 2 * math.cos(math.radians(a)), PCD / 2 * math.sin(math.radians(a))) for a in (45, 135, 225, 315)] pts = [(x, y) for _, x, y in pts_a] seat = -FLANGE_T body = body.cut(cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=seat + 2 * BRIDGE_LAYER) .pushPoints(pts).circle(M3_CLEAR / 2).extrude(FLANGE_T + 1)) for a, x, y in pts_a: slot = (cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=seat).center(x, y) .rect(M3_HEAD_CB + 0.4, M3_CLEAR).extrude(BRIDGE_LAYER).rotate((x, y, 0), (x, y, 1), a)) sq = (cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=seat + BRIDGE_LAYER).center(x, y) .rect(M3_CLEAR, M3_CLEAR).extrude(BRIDGE_LAYER + 0.01).rotate((x, y, 0), (x, y, 1), a)) body = body.cut(slot.intersect(cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=seat).center(x, y).circle(M3_HEAD_CB / 2).extrude(BRIDGE_LAYER))).cut(sq) body = body.cut(cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=seat) .pushPoints(pts).circle(M3_HEAD_CB / 2).extrude(-(CONE_H + 1))) # outer edge chamfer on the mating flange return body if __name__ == "__main__": out = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent part = build() cq.exporters.export(part, str(out / "mf6015_hex12_adapter.step")) cq.exporters.export(part, str(out / "mf6015_hex12_adapter.stl"), tolerance=0.02, angularTolerance=0.1) bb = part.val().BoundingBox() print("length %.1f mm, volume %.1f cm3, PETG mass ~%.0f g" % (bb.zlen, part.val().Volume() / 1000, part.val().Volume() / 1000 * 1.27))

#!/usr/bin/env bash # Every check that can run on a development machine, in one command. # # ./check.sh # all of it (~1.5 minutes) # ./check.sh elec pi # only these sections # sections: firmware | elec | pi | sim | site # # Several of these regenerate committed reports. This script snapshots those files # first, tells you if the fresh run disagrees with what is committed, and puts the # originals back, so running a check never leaves the working tree dirty. set -uo pipefail cd "$(dirname "$0")" ROOT="$PWD" PY="$ROOT/.venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$PY" ] || PY="$(command -v python3)" SECTIONS=("$@"); [ ${#SECTIONS[@]} -eq 0 ] && SECTIONS=(firmware elec pi sim site) want() { for s in "${SECTIONS[@]}"; do [ "$s" = "$1" ] && return 0; done; return 1; } PASS=(); FAIL=(); SKIP=(); DRIFT=() SNAP="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$SNAP"' EXIT # Generated files that the checks below overwrite. ARTIFACTS=(elec/erc_report.json elec/robot.net sim/robot_c.xml sim/robot_c_arena.xml sim/results/report.json sim/results/mission_log.npy sim/results/mission_marks.json) save_artifacts() { for f in "${ARTIFACTS[@]}"; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue mkdir -p "$SNAP/$(dirname "$f")"; cp -p "$f" "$SNAP/$f" done } restore_artifacts() { # report drift, then put the originals back for f in "${ARTIFACTS[@]}"; do [ -f "$SNAP/$f" ] || continue cmp -s "$SNAP/$f" "$f" || DRIFT+=("$f") cp -p "$SNAP/$f" "$f" done } # `bash -c` starts a fresh shell, which does NOT inherit the pipefail above: with `cmd | tail -3` # the status is tail's, so a crashing checker scored a pass. can_ground_check.py threw a KeyError # for a whole session that way. Every bash -c below is `bash -o pipefail -c` for that reason. run() { # run <name> <command...> local name="$1"; shift printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$name" if "$@"; then PASS+=("$name"); else FAIL+=("$name"); fi } save_artifacts if want firmware; then if command -v g++ >/dev/null; then run "firmware: host unit tests" firmware/esp32/test_host/run_tests.sh else SKIP+=("firmware: host unit tests (no g++)") fi fi if want elec; then run "elec: electrical rules check" bash -o pipefail -c "cd '$ROOT/elec' && '$PY' erc.py | tail -3" # test_erc.py calls erc.main(), which overwrites erc_report.json with the last # mutation case: re-run erc.py afterwards so the report matches the real wiring. run "elec: 8 wiring mutation tests" bash -o pipefail -c "cd '$ROOT/elec' && '$PY' test_erc.py && '$PY' erc.py >/dev/null" if [ -f cad_src/case/wiring_data.json ] || [ -f elec/wiring_data.json ]; then run "elec: CAN load and ground offset" bash -o pipefail -c "cd '$ROOT/elec' && '$PY' can_ground_check.py | tail -3" else SKIP+=("elec: CAN load and ground offset (needs wiring_data.json: cad_src/rebuild.sh)") fi fi if want pi; then if "$PY" -c "import pytest, aiohttp" 2>/dev/null; then run "pi: software test suite" bash -o pipefail -c "cd '$ROOT/pi' && '$PY' -m pytest -q tests" else SKIP+=("pi: software test suite (pip install 'pytest>=8' pytest-aiohttp)") fi fi if want site; then # The 3D viewer was dark for a long time because nothing ran it: module resolution can fail in a # way that produces a blank canvas and no visible error. tools/artifact_page.py builds the # self-contained copy, tools/check_viewer.mjs executes it against a DOM stub. if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then run "site: 3D viewer builds and runs" bash -o pipefail -c "cd '$ROOT' && '$PY' tools/artifact_page.py '$SNAP/viewer.html' >/dev/null && node tools/check_viewer.mjs '$SNAP/viewer.html' | grep -q 'RAN TO COMPLETION'" else SKIP+=("site: 3D viewer (no node)") fi fi if want sim; then run "sim: build the controller library" core/build_lib.sh if "$PY" -c "import mujoco" 2>/dev/null; then run "sim: regenerate the MuJoCo models" bash -o pipefail -c "cd '$ROOT/sim' && '$PY' build_model.py && '$PY' build_model.py --arena" run "sim: 30 randomised robots" bash -o pipefail -c "cd '$ROOT/sim' && '$PY' run_tests.py >/dev/null && '$PY' -c \" import json; r = json.load(open('results/report.json')) for k in ('stand-up from face-down', 'stand-up from back-down'): print(f' {k}: {r[k][\\\"success\\\"]}') print(' balance push recovery:', r['balance 10 s (randomised)']['push_recovered'])\"" else SKIP+=("sim: model and simulation tests (no mujoco: ml/setup_mac.sh)") fi fi restore_artifacts printf '\n\033[1m== summary\033[0m\n' for s in ${PASS[@]+"${PASS[@]}"}; do printf ' \033[32mpass\033[0m %s\n' "$s"; done for s in ${SKIP[@]+"${SKIP[@]}"}; do printf ' \033[33mskip\033[0m %s\n' "$s"; done for s in ${FAIL[@]+"${FAIL[@]}"}; do printf ' \033[31mFAIL\033[0m %s\n' "$s"; done if [ ${#DRIFT[@]} -gt 0 ]; then printf '\n \033[33mregenerated output differs from the committed copy:\033[0m\n' for f in "${DRIFT[@]}"; do printf ' %s\n' "$f"; done printf ' (the committed files were left untouched. Small last-digit differences are\n' printf ' normal across platforms; a changed success count is not.)\n' fi [ ${#FAIL[@]} -eq 0 ] || { printf '\n%d section(s) failed\n' "${#FAIL[@]}"; exit 1; } printf '\nall good\n'

"""CAN bus load / timing and ground offset between the ESP32's CAN transceiver and the motors' CAN reference. Lengths and gauges come from the harness model (case/wiring_data.json).""" import json, os, sys HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) for _p in (os.path.join(HERE, os.pardir, "cad_src", "case"), "/home/claude/case"): if os.path.isdir(_p): sys.path.append(_p) # robot_paths: this machine's layout import robot_paths as RP WD = json.load(open(RP.artifact("wiring_data.json"))) OHM_PER_M = {12: 0.00521, 16: 0.0132, 20: 0.0333, 22: 0.0530, 24: 0.0842, 26: 0.134} def wire(h, sig): for x in WD: if x["name"] == h: for c in x["conds"]: if c["sig"] == sig: return c["L"] / 100 * OHM_PER_M[c["awg"]], c["L"], c["awg"] raise KeyError((h, sig)) out = {} # ---- CAN timing (1 Mbit/s, standard 11-bit frames, 8 data bytes) ---- BIT = 1e-6 def frame_bits(n=8, worst=True): base = 47 + 8 * n # SOF..EOF incl. CRC delimiter, ACK, EOF (no IFS) stuff = (34 + 8 * n - 1) // 4 if worst else 0 return base + stuff + 3 # + intermission CYCLE = 0.002 # control period (500 Hz) f = frame_bits() on = 3 * f * BIT # 0x280 torque frame + 2 replies off = 4 * f * BIT # 2 x 0x9C + 2 replies (motors off) out["can"] = dict(frame_us_worst=round(f * BIT * 1e6), per_cycle_on_us=round(on * 1e6), load_on_pct=round(100 * on / CYCLE), per_cycle_off_us=round(off * 1e6), load_off_pct=round(100 * off / CYCLE), retransmits_that_fit_in_a_cycle=int((CYCLE - on) / ((frame_bits() + 23) * BIT)), bus_off_recovery_ms=round(128 * 11 * BIT * 1e3, 2), can_timeout_ms=20, note="Replies are read at the start of the next cycle (1 cycle of latency, modelled in the sim). Same # discipline as the wiring mutations: break each rule and the check has to notice. """Linear static FEA (CalculiX) of the lower body under motor loads. Usage: python3 fea.py old|new Geometry: body_case.build_body() cut to the lower part (z -36..36), tet10 mesh (gmsh). Loads per motor, through the 4 M2.5 screws (hole wall + area under the head): - reaction torque T about the axle (both motors same direction: worst for the body) - wheel force Fz (ground pushing up, bumps/landing), moved from the wheel centre to the wall -> force + bending moment about x Fixed: the 4 floor insert bosses of the front panel / back cover screws (the only link to the shell). """ import sys, os, subprocess, json, numpy as np HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HERE, "..", "cad_scripts")) import cadquery as cq, body_case as bc, gmsh VAR = sys.argv[1] T_NMM = float(os.environ.get("T", 2300.0)) # 2.3 N.m: 16.5 A x 0.14 N.m/A, motor peak FZ = float(os.environ.get("FZ", 25.0)) # N per wheel: ~3 g on half the robot's weight E, NU = 2000.0, 0.38 # PETG, MPa H = float(os.environ.get("H", 1.4)) # mesh size at the motor walls (mm) WITH_SHELF = VAR == "reinf" and os.environ.get("NOSHELF", "0") != "1" SHELF = os.environ.get("SHELF", "0") == "1" # 1: the battery shelf holds the rail tops (y, z) OUT = os.path.join(HERE, "out", VAR) + ("_noshelf" if VAR == "reinf" and not WITH_SHELF else "") + ("_shelf" if SHELF else "") + os.environ.get("TAG", ""); os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True) # the two tray bosses touch the motor walls tangentially (r 4 at y 13 vs wall at 17): a zero-width sliver # that no mesher handles; merge them 1 mm into the wall for the analysis (no effect away from the floor) bc.FLOOR_TRAY_PTS = [(-24.0, -12.0), (21.0, 12.0)] if VAR == "old": bc.SLOT_W, bc.SLOT_Z = 19.0, (13.0, bc.SHELF_Z + 0.1) body = bc.build_body().val() ZC = 36.0 # the floor + motor-walls block is a separate solid from the shell (the wheel wells cut the floor off) lower = [s for s in body.Solids() if s.BoundingBox().zmin < -30][0] if WITH_SHELF: # shelf screwed to the wall tops: modelled as bonded lower = lower.fuse(bc.build_shelf().val()).clean() cq.exporters.export(cq.Workplane().add(lower), f"{OUT}/lower.step") # ---------------- mesh ---------------- gmsh.initialize(); gmsh.option.setNumber("General.Terminal", 0) for k_, v_ in [("Geometry.OCCFixDegenerated", 1), ("Geometry.OCCFixSmallEdges", 1), ("Geometry.OCCFixSmallFaces", 1), ("Geometry.OCCSewFaces", 1)]: gmsh.option.setNumber(k_, v_) gmsh.model.occ.importShapes(f"{OUT}/lower.step"); gmsh.model.occ.healShapes(); gmsh.model.occ.removeAllDuplicates(); gmsh.model.occ.synchronize() f = gmsh.model.mesh.field b1 = f.add("Box"); f.setNumber(b1, "VIn", H); f.setNumber(b1, "VOut", 3.2) f.setNumber(b1, "XMin", -32); f.setNumber(b1, "XMax", 29); f.setNumber(b1, "YMin", -26); f.setNumber(b1, "YMax", 26) f.setNumber(b1, "ZMin", -36); f.setNumber(b1, "ZMax", 37); f.setNumber(b1, "Thickness", 8) f.setAsBackgroundMesh(b1) gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.MeshSizeExtendFromBoundary", 0); gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.MeshSizeFromPoints", 0) gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.MeshSizeFromCurvature", 0) gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.ElementOrder", 2); gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.HighOrderOptimize", 0); gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.SecondOrderLinear", 1) gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.Algorithm3D", int(os.environ.get("ALG3", 1))) gmsh.model.mesh.generate(3) tag, xyz, _ = gmsh.model.mesh.getNodes() X = xyz.reshape(-1, 3); idx = {int(t): i for i, t in enumerate(tag)} et, etags, enodes = gmsh.model.mesh.getElements(3) k = list(et).index(11) # 10-node tet tets = np.array([idx[int(n)] for n in enodes[k]]).reshape(-1, 10) gmsh.finalize() print(f"{VAR}: {len(X)} nodes, {len(tets)} tet10") # ---------------- BCs and loads ---------------- # supports: the 4 floor bosses where the front panel and back cover screw on (M3 inserts, y +-40, z -28.5). # The panels tie this block to the upper shell; they are treated as rigid. zb = bc.Z_FLOOR + 3.5 ri = bc.INSERT_D / 2 fixed = np.where((np.abs(np.hypot(np.abs(X[:, 1]) - 40.0, X[:, 2] - zb) - ri) < 0.08) & ((X[:, 0] > bc.X_IN_F - bc.INS_M3[1] - 0.1) | (X[:, 0] < bc.X_BACK + bc.INS_M3[1] + 0.1)))[0] rails = np.where(X[:, 2] > bc.SHELF_Z + bc.RAIL_H - 0.05)[0] if SHELF else np.array([], int) print("fixed nodes", len(fixed), "rail nodes", len(rails)) F = np.zeros_like(X) HOLES = [(-10, -10), (10, -10), (10, 10), (-10, 10)] rh = bc.M25_CLEAR / 2 for s in (1, -1): yin = s * bc.GAP_HALF # inner wall face (screw heads) ywall = s * (bc.GAP_HALF + bc.MWALL_T / 2) yw = s * (bc.WHEEL_IN_Y + bc.WHEEL_W / 2) d = yw - ywall for (xc, zc) in HOLES: rr = np.hypot(X[:, 0] - xc, X[:, 2] - zc) inwall = (s * X[:, 1] > bc.GAP_HALF - 0.05) & (s * X[:, 1] < bc.GAP_HALF + bc.MWALL_T + 0.05) shank = inwall & (np.abs(rr - rh) < 0.08) head = (np.abs(X[:, 1] - yin) < 0.05) & (rr > rh - 0.05) & (rr < 2.4) sel = np.where(shank | head)[0] fh = np.array([T_NMM / (4 * 200.0) * zc, 0.0, -T_NMM / (4 * 200.0) * xc]) # sum r x F = T about y fh += np.array([0.0, -d * FZ * zc / 400.0, FZ / 4]) # Fz + moment d*Fz about x F[sel] += fh / len(sel) assert abs(F[:, 2].sum() - 2 * FZ) < 1e-6 # ---------------- CalculiX ---------------- with open(f"{OUT}/job.inp", "w") as o: o.write("*NODE, NSET=NALL\n") for i, p in enumerate(X): o.write(f"{i+1},{p[0]:.6f},{p[1]:.6f},{p[2]:.6f}\n") o.write("*ELEMENT, TYPE=C3D10, ELSET=EALL\n") perm = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 8] # gmsh -> abaqus/ccx edge-node order for j, t in enumerate(tets): o.write(f"{j+1}," + ",".join(str(t[p] + 1) for p in perm) + "\n") o.write("*NSET, NSET=FIX\n" + "\n".join(str(i + 1) for i in fixed) + "\n") o.write(f"*MATERIAL, NAME=PETG\n*ELASTIC\n{E},{NU}\n*SOLID SECTION, ELSET=EALL, MATERIAL=PETG\n") if len(rails): o.write("*NSET, NSET=RAIL\n" + "\n".join(str(i + 1) for i in rails) + "\n") o.write("*STEP\n*STATIC\n*BOUNDARY\nFIX,1,3,0\n" + ("RAIL,2,3,0\n" if len(rails) else "") + "*CLOAD\n") for i in np.where(np.abs(F).sum(1) > 0)[0]: for c in range(3): if F[i, c] != 0: o.write(f"{i+1},{c+1},{F[i, c]:.6e}\n") o.write("*NODE FILE\nU\n*EL FILE\nS\n*END STEP\n") subprocess.run(["ccx", "-i", "job"], cwd=OUT, check=True, stdout=open(f"{OUT}/ccx.log", "w")) # ---------------- read results ---------------- def read_frd(path, name, ncomp): out = {}; on = False for line in open(path): if line.startswith(" -4") and name in line: on = True; continue if on: if line.startswith(" -3"): break if line.startswith(" -1"): n = int(line[3:13]); out[n] = [float(line[13 + 12 * c:25 + 12 * c]) for c in range(ncomp)] a = np.zeros((len(X), ncomp)) for n, v in out.items(): a[n - 1] = v return a U = read_frd(f"{OUT}/job.frd", "DISP", 3) S = read_frd(f"{OUT}/job.frd", "STRESS", 6) # xx yy zz xy yz zx sx, sy, sz, txy, tyz, tzx = S.T vm = np.sqrt(0.5 * ((sx - sy) ** 2 + (sy - sz) ** 2 + (sz - sx) ** 2) + 3 * (txy ** 2 + tyz ** 2 + tzx ** 2)) np.savez_compressed(f"{OUT}/res.npz", X=X, tets=tets[:, :4], U=U, S=S, vm=vm, F=F) # exclude the load-introduction points (local bearing under the screws, real but not a structural weakness) near = np.zeros(len(X), bool) for (xc, zc) in HOLES: near |= (np.hypot(X[:, 0] - xc, X[:, 2] - zc) < 3.2) & (np.abs(X[:, 1]) < 25) def region(m): i = np.where(m & ~near)[0]; j = i[np.argmax(vm[i])] return dict(vm=round(float(vm[j]), 2), sx_tension=round(float(sx[i].max()), 2), at=[round(float(v), 1) for v in X[j]]) wall = (np.abs(X[:, 1]) > 16.9) & (np.abs(X[:, 1]) < 24.1) res = { "variant": VAR, "nodes": len(X), "T_Nm": T_NMM / 1000, "Fz_N": FZ, "max_disp_mm": round(float(np.linalg.norm(U, axis=1).max()), 4), "motor_wall_twist_deg": None, "everywhere": region(np.ones(len(X), bool)), "motor_walls": region(wall), "wall_above_axle_z12_36": region(wall & (X[:, 2] > 12)), "wall_floor_junction": region(wall & (X[:, 2] < -27)), "floor_bosses": region((np.abs(np.abs(X[:, 1]) - 40) < 8) & (X[:, 2] < -20)), "rest_of_body": region(~wall & (X[:, 2] < bc.SHELF_Z - 0.05)), "shelf": region(X[:, 2] > bc.SHELF_Z + 0.05) if (X[:, 2] > bc.SHELF_Z + 0.05).any() else None, "screw_bearing_max": round(float(vm[near].max()), 2), } # rotation of the motor mount (rigid-body fit of the hole-node displacements) -> how much the motor axis tilts for s in (1, -1): m = (s * X[:, 1] > bc.GAP_HALF - 0.05) & (s * X[:, 1] < bc.GAP_HALF + bc.MWALL_T + 0.05) & near P = X[m] - X[m].mean(0); D = U[m] - U[m].mean(0) A = np.zeros((3 * len(P), 3)); b = D.reshape(-1) for q, p in enumerate(P): # D = w x p A[3 * q] = [0, p[2], -p[1]]; A[3 * q + 1] = [-p[2], 0, p[0]]; A[3 * q + 2] = [p[1], -p[0], 0] w = np.linalg.lstsq(A, b, rcond=None)[0] res[f"mount_rotation_deg_side{s:+d}"] = [round(float(np.degrees(v)), 4) for v in w] res[f"mount_shift_mm_side{s:+d}"] = [round(float(v), 4) for v in U[m].mean(0)] del res["motor_wall_twist_deg"] json.dump(res, open(f"{OUT}/summary.json", "w"), indent=1) print(json.dumps(res, indent=1))

import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg") import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from render import surface, draw def load(d): r = np.load(f"out/{d}/res.npz"); return r["X"], surface(r["tets"]), r["vm"] VMAX = 20.0 cases = [("new", "Before: shelf only sliding on rails (loose)\nmax 20.5 MPa · motor axis tilts 3.3°"), ("reinf", "Now: shelf screwed, fillets, ribs, deeper body\nmax 5.4 MPa · motor axis tilts 0.24°")] fig = plt.figure(figsize=(7.4, 9.0), dpi=130) for i, (d, t) in enumerate(cases): X, F, vm = load(d) ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 2 * i + 1, projection="3d"); draw(ax, X, F, vm, 28, -128, VMAX, title=t) ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 2 * i + 2, projection="3d"); draw(ax, X, F, vm, -32, 58, VMAX, title="from below") sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(cmap="turbo", norm=plt.Normalize(0, VMAX)) cb = fig.colorbar(sm, ax=fig.axes, orientation="horizontal", fraction=0.03, pad=0.03) cb.set_label("von Mises (MPa) · peak torque 2.3 N·m + 25 N per wheel · PETG layer bond ≈ 20–30 MPa") plt.savefig("fea_before_after.png", bbox_inches="tight"); print("ok")

"""Render von Mises stress on the outer surface of a CalculiX result (res.npz).""" import sys, numpy as np, matplotlib matplotlib.use("Agg") import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d.art3d import Poly3DCollection def surface(tets): f = np.concatenate([tets[:, [0, 2, 1]], tets[:, [0, 1, 3]], tets[:, [1, 2, 3]], tets[:, [0, 3, 2]]]) k = np.sort(f, 1); _, idx, cnt = np.unique(k, axis=0, return_index=True, return_counts=True) return f[idx[cnt == 1]] def draw(ax, X, F, vm, elev, azim, vmax, lim=None, title=""): if lim is not None: c = X[F].mean(1); m = np.all((c >= lim[0]) & (c <= lim[1]), 1); F = F[m] tri = X[F]; val = vm[F].mean(1) n = np.cross(tri[:, 1] - tri[:, 0], tri[:, 2] - tri[:, 0]); n /= np.linalg.norm(n, axis=1)[:, None] + 1e-12 e, a = np.radians(elev), np.radians(azim) view = np.array([np.cos(e) * np.cos(a), np.cos(e) * np.sin(a), np.sin(e)]) shade = 0.55 + 0.45 * np.abs(n @ view) col = plt.cm.turbo(np.clip(val / vmax, 0, 1)); col[:, :3] *= shade[:, None] depth = tri.mean(1) @ view; o = np.argsort(depth) ax.add_collection3d(Poly3DCollection(tri[o], facecolors=col[o], edgecolors="none", linewidths=0)) lo, hi = (X.min(0), X.max(0)) if lim is None else (np.array(lim[0]), np.array(lim[1])) ax.set_xlim(lo[0], hi[0]); ax.set_ylim(lo[1], hi[1]); ax.set_zlim(lo[2], hi[2]) ax.set_box_aspect(hi - lo); ax.view_init(elev, azim); ax.set_axis_off(); ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10) if __name__ == "__main__": pass

"""Virtual LK MF6015 motors on the MuJoCo robot, shared by the QEMU test (hil/run_hil.py) and the real-CAN bench (bench/bench_hil.py). LK CAN protocol V2: 0x88 on / 0x80 off (reply = echo of the command), 0x9C read state 2 and 0x280 multi-motor torque (replies [cmd, temp, iq, speed dps, encoder] from 0x141/0x142).""" import math, os, struct, sys, pathlib import numpy as np, mujoco ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "sim")) from botsim import BotSim, CTRL_DT, KT, I_MAX, quat_pitch # noqa: E402,F401 (plant, motor model, IMU model) ENC_BITS = int(os.environ.get("ENC_BITS", "16")) ENC_RANGE = 1 << ENC_BITS ID_L, ID_R, ID_MULTI = 0x141, 0x142, 0x280 DIR = {ID_L: +1, ID_R: -1} # must match config.h DIR_LEFT/DIR_RIGHT IQ_FULL, IQ_MAX = 16.5, 2048 def crc(p): c = 0 for b in p: c = (((c << 1) | (c >> 7)) & 0xFF) ^ b return c def frame(t, payload): body = bytes([t, len(payload)]) + payload return b"\xA5\x5A" + body + bytes([crc(body)]) class Plant(BotSim): """MuJoCo robot driven by external motor commands (the firmware), with the LK drive model of botsim.""" def __init__(self, seed, randomize=True): super().__init__(seed=seed, randomize=randomize) self.on = {ID_L: False, ID_R: False} self.iq_cmd = {ID_L: 0, ID_R: 0} self.t_fw = None; self.rem = 0.0 self.push = None; self.push_until = 0.0 self.hold = None self.trace = [] def joint_w(self, side): return self.d.qvel[self.m.jnt_dofadr[self.m.joint(f"{side}_hinge").id]] def advance(self, dt): n = int((dt + self.rem) / self.m.opt.timestep + 1e-9) self.rem = dt + self.rem - n * self.m.opt.timestep for _ in range(n): tq = [] for mid, side in ((ID_L, "left"), (ID_R, "right")): tau = DIR[mid] * self.iq_cmd[mid] * IQ_FULL / IQ_MAX * KT if self.on[mid] else 0.0 tq.append(self.motor(tau, self.joint_w(side))) self.d.ctrl[:] = tq if self.push is not None and self.t < self.push_until: self.d.xfrc_applied[self.ch, :3] = self.push else: self.d.xfrc_applied[self.ch, :3] = 0 mujoco.mj_step(self.m, self.d) if self.hold is not None: self.d.qpos[:] = self.hold; self.d.qvel[:] = 0; mujoco.mj_forward(self.m, self.d) self.t += self.m.opt.timestep self.trace.append((self.t, quat_pitch(self.d.qpos[3:7]), float(self.d.qpos[0]), float(self.d.qpos[1]), self.on[ID_L], self.iq_cmd[ID_L], self.iq_cmd[ID_R])) def imu(self): s = self.sense() return struct.pack("<6f", s.ax, s.ay, s.az, s.gx, s.gy, s.gz) def reply(self, mid, cmd): """LK V2 reply: [cmd, temp, iq, speed dps, encoder] (0xA1 / 0x9C).""" s, sd = self.d.sensordata, self.sid q = s[sd["ql"]] if mid == ID_L else s[sd["qr"]] # wheel angle relative to the body, robot-forward + w = s[sd["wl"]] if mid == ID_L else s[sd["wr"]] raw = DIR[mid] * q enc = int(round((raw / (2 * math.pi)) * ENC_RANGE)) % ENC_RANGE dps = int(round(math.degrees(DIR[mid] * w))) iq = int(self.iq_cmd[mid] if self.on[mid] else 0) return struct.pack("<BbhhH", cmd, 30, iq, max(-32768, min(32767, dps)), enc) class VirtualLK: """Answers LK frames for motors 1 (0x141) and 2 (0x142) from the plant's state. handle() returns the reply frames.""" def __init__(self, plant): self.p = plant self.mute_until = -1.0 # plant time until which the motors are silent (CAN unplugged) self.rx = 0; self.tx = 0 def handle(self, cid, d): P = self.p; d = bytes(d) self.rx += 1 if P.t < self.mute_until or len(d) < 8: return [] cmd = d[0]; out = [] if cid == ID_MULTI: a, b = struct.unpack("<hh", d[:4]) P.iq_cmd[ID_L], P.iq_cmd[ID_R] = max(-IQ_MAX, min(IQ_MAX, a)), max(-IQ_MAX, min(IQ_MAX, b)) out = [(mid, P.reply(mid, 0xA1)) for mid in (ID_L, ID_R)] elif cid in (ID_L, ID_R): if cmd == 0x88: P.on[cid] = True if cmd == 0x80: P.on[cid] = False; P.iq_cmd[cid] = 0 if cmd in (0x80, 0x88): out = [(cid, d)] # LK manual: reply = the command itself elif cmd == 0x9C: out = [(cid, P.reply(cid, 0x9C))] elif cmd == 0xA1: # single-motor torque (probe tool) P.iq_cmd[cid] = max(-IQ_MAX, min(IQ_MAX, struct.unpack("<h", d[4:6])[0])); P.on[cid] = True out = [(cid, P.reply(cid, 0xA1))] self.tx += len(out) return out

"""Hardware-in-the-loop test: the real ESP32-S3 firmware (env esp32s3_sim) runs in Espressif QEMU against the MuJoCo robot. The Pi side is the real pi/robot/link.py. QEMU UART1 -> Pi link (921600 protocol of link_proto.h), driven here through pi/robot/link.Link QEMU UART0 -> this host: virtual LK MF6015 motors (CAN frames, LK protocol V2) + IMU samples, in lock-step (console text shares UART0; bytes outside frames are written to the console log): every control cycle the firmware sends its own clock; the physics advances by exactly that much. Usage: python3 run_hil.py [scenario ...] (scenarios: standup_face standup_back balance_push drive cmd_timeout can_loss) ENC_BITS=14 python3 run_hil.py ... -> virtual motors with a 14-bit encoder (the LK manual allows 14/15/16 bit) """ import math, os, socket, struct, subprocess, sys, threading, time, json, pathlib, collections import numpy as np, mujoco ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "sim")); sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "pi")); sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "hil")) from lkbus import Plant, VirtualLK, crc, frame, quat_pitch, CTRL_DT, ID_L, ID_R # noqa: E402 (plant + virtual motors) from robot.link import Link, MODE_VELOCITY, MODE_TURN_BY # noqa: E402 (the Pi's own link code) QEMU = os.environ.get("QEMU", "/opt/dl/qemu/qemu/bin/qemu-system-xtensa") FLASH = os.environ.get("FLASH", "/tmp/flash_sim.bin") class SockPort: """read(n)/write(b) over a socket, for pi/robot/link.Link.""" def __init__(self, s): self.s = s; self.s.settimeout(0.01) def read(self, n): try: return self.s.recv(n) except (socket.timeout, BlockingIOError): return b"" except OSError: return b"" def write(self, b): try: self.s.sendall(b) except OSError: pass class Host: def __init__(self, seed=1, randomize=True, log_dir="/tmp/hil"): self.plant = Plant(seed, randomize) self.vlk = VirtualLK(self.plant) self.log_dir = pathlib.Path(log_dir); self.log_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True) self.can_mute_until = -1.0 self.events = []; self.telem = [] self.cycles = 0; self.dts = []; self.host_ms = []; self.wall = [] self.stop = False # ------------------------------------------------------------ QEMU + sockets def start(self, tag): self.tag = tag srv = [] for _ in range(2): s = socket.socket(); s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1); s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)); s.listen(1); srv.append(s) p1, p2 = (s.getsockname()[1] for s in srv) self.console = self.log_dir / f"{tag}_console.log" cmd = [QEMU, "-nographic", "-accel", os.environ.get("QEMU_ACCEL", "tcg"), "-machine", "esp32s3", *os.environ.get("QEMU_EXTRA", "-icount shift=2,sleep=on,align=off").split(), "-m", "8M", "-global", "ssi_psram.is_octal=true", "-global", "ssi_psram.size_mbytes=8", "-drive", f"file={self.flash_copy()},if=mtd,format=raw", "-serial", f"tcp:127.0.0.1:{p2},nodelay=on", "-serial", f"tcp:127.0.0.1:{p1},nodelay=on", "-monitor", "none"] self.con = open(self.console, "wb") self.q = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL) for s in srv: s.settimeout(20) self.bus, _ = srv[1].accept(); self.pi_sock, _ = srv[0].accept() self.bus.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_NODELAY, 1) self.link = Link(SockPort(self.pi_sock), on_event=lambda txt: self.events.append((self.plant.t, txt))) self.th = threading.Thread(target=self.bus_loop, daemon=True); self.th.start() def flash_copy(self): dst = self.log_dir / f"flash_{os.getpid()}.bin" if not dst.exists(): dst.write_bytes(pathlib.Path(FLASH).read_bytes()) # fresh NVS every scenario return dst def close(self): self.stop = True try: self.con.flush() except Exception: pass try: self.q.terminate(); self.q.wait(5) except Exception: self.q.kill() for p in self.log_dir.glob(f"flash_{os.getpid()}.bin"): p.unlink() # ------------------------------------------------------------ virtual CAN bus + IMU (lock-step) def bus_loop(self): buf = bytearray(); P = self.plant self.bus.settimeout(0.5) while not self.stop: try: data = self.bus.recv(4096) except socket.timeout: continue except OSError: break if not data: break buf += data out = bytearray() while True: i = buf.find(b"\xA5\x5A") if i < 0: self.con.write(bytes(buf[:-1])); del buf[:-1]; break if i: self.con.write(bytes(buf[:i])); del buf[:i] if len(buf) < 4: break n = 4 + buf[3] + 1 if len(buf) < n: break body = bytes(buf[2:n - 1]); ok = crc(body) == buf[n - 1] t, p = body[0], body[2:] del buf[:n] if not ok: continue if t == ord("C"): cid, dlc, d = struct.unpack("<IB8s3x", p) out += self.on_can(cid, d) elif t == ord("S"): t_us, = struct.unpack("<I", p) w0 = time.perf_counter() dt = CTRL_DT if P.t_fw is None else ((t_us - P.t_fw) & 0xFFFFFFFF) * 1e-6 P.t_fw = t_us if self.cycles > 0: P.advance(min(dt, 0.05)); self.dts.append(dt) self.cycles += 1 out += frame(ord("I"), P.imu()) self.host_ms.append(1e3 * (time.perf_counter() - w0)); self.wall.append(w0) if out: self.bus.sendall(bytes(out)) def on_can(self, cid, d): self.vlk.mute_until = self.can_mute_until return b"".join(frame(ord("C"), struct.pack("<IB8s3x", i, 8, data)) for i, data in self.vlk.handle(cid, d)) # ------------------------------------------------------------ Pi side def run_for(self, seconds, **cmd): """Keep sending Pi commands at 20 Hz (like the Pi brain) while the physics advances `seconds`.""" t_end = self.plant.t + seconds; deadline = time.time() + seconds * 40 + 30 while self.plant.t < t_end and time.time() < deadline and self.q.poll() is None: if cmd.get("silent") is not True: self.link.send(**{k: v for k, v in cmd.items() if k != "silent"}) self.telem.append((self.plant.t, self.link.telem)) time.sleep(0.05 * max(1.0, self.slowdown())) return self.plant.t >= t_end def slowdown(self): """Wall time per simulated second (QEMU runs the firmware in real time; the host keeps up).""" return 1.0 def wait_boot(self, timeout=30): t0 = time.time() while time.time() - t0 < timeout: if any("state" in e for _, e in self.events): return True time.sleep(0.05) return False # ---------------------------------------------------------------- scenarios def summary(h, extra=None): tr = np.array([(t, p, x, y) for t, p, x, y, *_ in h.plant.trace]) if h.plant.trace else np.zeros((1, 4)) st = [(round(t, 3), e) for t, e in h.events if e.startswith("state")] dts = np.array(h.dts) if h.dts else np.array([0]) r = dict(cycles=h.cycles, sim_s=round(h.plant.t, 2), dt_ms_median=round(1e3 * float(np.median(dts)), 3), dt_ms_p99=round(1e3 * float(np.percentile(dts, 99)), 3), dt_ms_max=round(1e3 * float(dts.max()), 2), host_ms_p99=round(float(np.percentile(h.host_ms, 99)), 3) if h.host_ms else None, host_ms_max=round(float(max(h.host_ms)), 2) if h.host_ms else None, states=st, final_state=h.link.telem.state_name, motor_fault=h.link.telem.motor_fault, armed=h.link.telem.armed, batt_low=h.link.telem.battery_low, final_pitch_deg=round(math.degrees(tr[-1, 1]), 1)) if extra: r.update(extra) return r def standup(seed, side): h = Host(seed); h.plant.place(1.8 * side); h.start(f"standup_{'face' if side > 0 else 'back'}_{seed}") ok = h.wait_boot() h.run_for(0.5, arm=False) # booted, lying, disarmed h.run_for(4.0, arm=True) # arm: auto stand-up tr = np.array([(t, p) for t, p, *_ in h.plant.trace]) t_arm = tr[0, 0] + 0.5 up = [t for t, e in h.events if "BALANCE" in e] r = summary(h, dict(booted=ok, stood_up=bool(up), t_standup_s=round(up[0] - t_arm, 2) if up else None, upright_at_end=bool(abs(tr[-1, 1]) < 0.3))) h.close(); return r def balance_push(seed): h = Host(seed); h.plant.place(0); h.start(f"balance_{seed}") h.wait_boot() h.plant.hold = h.plant.d.qpos.copy() # a hand holds it upright while it boots and arms h.run_for(0.5, arm=True); h.plant.hold = None h.run_for(2.0) x0 = h.plant.d.qpos[0] res = [] for k, imp in enumerate((1.0, -1.0, 1.5)): h.plant.push = np.array([imp / 0.1, 0, 0]); h.plant.push_until = h.plant.t + 0.1 h.run_for(3.0) res.append(dict(impulse_Ns=imp, upright=bool(abs(quat_pitch(h.plant.d.qpos[3:7])) < 0.3), state=h.link.telem.state_name)) tr = np.array([(t, p, x) for t, p, x, *_ in h.plant.trace]) calm = tr[(tr[:, 0] > tr[0, 0] + 0.6) & (tr[:, 0] < tr[0, 0] + 2.4)] r = summary(h, dict(pushes=res, still_pitch_std_deg=round(math.degrees(float(calm[:, 1].std())), 3) if len(calm) else None, still_drift_mm=round(1e3 * float(np.ptp(calm[:, 2]))) if len(calm) else None)) h.close(); return r def drive(seed): h = Host(seed); h.plant.place(0); h.start(f"drive_{seed}") h.wait_boot() h.plant.hold = h.plant.d.qpos.copy() # a hand holds it upright while it boots and arms h.run_for(0.5, arm=True); h.plant.hold = None h.run_for(1.0) p0 = h.plant.d.qpos[:2].copy() h.run_for(3.0, v=0.5) v_true = [(t, x) for t, _, x, *_ in h.plant.trace[-250:]] v_meas = (v_true[-1][1] - v_true[0][1]) / (v_true[-1][0] - v_true[0][0]) h.run_for(2.5, v=0.0) p1 = h.plant.d.qpos[:2].copy() odo = h.link.telem h.link.send(mode=MODE_TURN_BY, angle=math.pi / 2, new_turn=True) h.run_for(3.0, mode=MODE_TURN_BY, angle=math.pi / 2) yaw = h.plant.true_yaw() r = summary(h, dict(speed_cmd=0.5, speed_true=round(v_meas, 3), dist_true_m=round(float(np.linalg.norm(p1 - p0)), 3), odo_x_m=round(odo.x, 3), turn_cmd_deg=90, yaw_true_deg=round(math.degrees(yaw), 1), upright=bool(abs(quat_pitch(h.plant.d.qpos[3:7])) < 0.3))) h.close(); return r def cmd_timeout(seed): """Pi goes silent while driving at 0.5 m/s: the firmware must stop driving within ~0.3 s and keep balancing.""" h = Host(seed); h.plant.place(0); h.start(f"cmd_timeout_{seed}") h.wait_boot() h.plant.hold = h.plant.d.qpos.copy() # a hand holds it upright while it boots and arms h.run_for(0.5, arm=True); h.plant.hold = None h.run_for(1.0); h.run_for(2.0, v=0.5) t_cut = h.plant.t h.run_for(4.0, silent=True) tr = np.array([(t, x) for t, _, x, *_ in h.plant.trace]) after = tr[tr[:, 0] > t_cut + 2.5] v_end = (after[-1, 1] - after[0, 1]) / (after[-1, 0] - after[0, 0]) if len(after) > 2 else None r = summary(h, dict(speed_after_silence=round(v_end, 3) if v_end is not None else None, upright=bool(abs(quat_pitch(h.plant.d.qpos[3:7])) < 0.3))) h.close(); return r def can_loss(seed): """CAN unplugged for 100 ms while balancing: firmware must declare a motor fault and switch the motors off.""" h = Host(seed); h.plant.place(0); h.start(f"can_loss_{seed}") h.wait_boot() h.plant.hold = h.plant.d.qpos.copy() # a hand holds it upright while it boots and arms h.run_for(0.5, arm=True); h.plant.hold = None h.run_for(1.5) t_cut = h.plant.t; h.can_mute_until = t_cut + 0.1 h.run_for(1.0) t_off = [t for t, _, _, _, on, *_ in h.plant.trace if t > t_cut + 0.1 and not on] fault = [t - t_cut for t, e in h.events if t > t_cut and ("fault" in e or "FAULT" in e or "DISARMED" in e)] r = summary(h, dict(fault_flag=h.link.telem.motor_fault, motors_on_at_end=bool(h.plant.on[ID_L] or h.plant.on[ID_R]), reaction_s=round(fault[0], 3) if fault else None, motors_off_after_bus_back_s=round(t_off[0] - t_cut - 0.1, 3) if t_off else None)) h.close(); return r SCEN = {"standup_face": lambda s: standup(s, +1), "standup_back": lambda s: standup(s, -1), "balance_push": balance_push, "drive": drive, "cmd_timeout": cmd_timeout, "can_loss": can_loss} if __name__ == "__main__": names = sys.argv[1:] or list(SCEN) seeds = [int(x) for x in os.environ.get("SEEDS", "1").split(",")] allr = {} for n in names: for s in seeds: t0 = time.time() r = SCEN[n](s); r["wall_s"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1) allr[f"{n}_{s}"] = r print(n, s, json.dumps(r), flush=True) out = pathlib.Path(os.environ.get("OUT", "/tmp/hil/results.json")) out.write_text(json.dumps(allr, indent=1))

# Learned stand-up (reinforcement learning) Goal: replace the hand-tuned stand-up kick (lying → upright) with a small neural network trained in the simulator, because the taller V1.1 body made the hand-tuned one fail ~15 % of the time (the kick reaches the motors' speed limit before the body is up). Balancing stays with the LQR controller; only the push from lying until the catch (|pitch| < 20°) is learned. The hand-tuned stand-up stays as the fallback. ## How it fits together | Piece | What it does | |---|---| | `core/controller.cpp` | `standup_mode`: 0 = hand-tuned (default), 1 = neural policy, 2 = torque from outside (training). The policy's inputs come from `Controller::standup_obs()`, the same function in the sim and on the robot. | | `core/standup_policy.hpp` | The policy as plain C++ arrays (generated). The placeholder in git has no policy, so mode 1 falls back to 0. | | `ml/standup_env.py` | Gymnasium environment around `sim/botsim.py` (MuJoCo + the real C++ controller). Every episode is a randomised robot: mass, centre of mass, inertia, grip, battery, torque gain, CAN delay, IMU bias. | | `ml/train.py` | PPO (stable-baselines3), one simulator per CPU core. | | `ml/evaluate.py` | Hand-tuned vs learned on the 60 test robots of `sim/run_tests.py`. | | `ml/export_policy.py` | Trained model → `core/standup_policy.hpp` (checks C++ math = PyTorch). | Policy: tanh MLP 6 → 64 → 64 → 1, one action every 10 ms = push for both motors (fraction of 2 × 2.3 N·m). Inputs (side-normalised): pitch, pitch rate, wheel speed, time, battery voltage, last action. Reward: progress towards upright, small costs for fast wheels and big pushes, +10 if the normal controller still holds it upright 1 s after the catch (minus distance travelled), −5 for falling over / running away. ## On the Mac ```bash git clone https://github.com/tuanito/2-wheel-balanced-bot && cd 2-wheel-balanced-bot ml/setup_mac.sh # venv + MuJoCo + PPO, builds sim/libbot.dylib ml/run_training.sh --steps 2000000 # the whole loop below; tensorboard --logdir ml/runs ``` `run_training.sh` is these steps, in order. The rebuild before the last line is the one to remember: without it `--compiled` measures the *previous* policy and still prints a plausible number. ```bash source .venv/bin/activate python ml/evaluate.py # baseline: the hand-tuned stand-up python ml/train.py --steps 2000000 # uses all cores but one python ml/evaluate.py ml/runs/standup/best.zip # learned vs hand-tuned python ml/export_policy.py ml/runs/standup/best.zip core/build_lib.sh # rebuild with the exported policy python ml/evaluate.py --compiled # the exported C++ policy inside the controller (what the robot runs) ``` Training time on an M-series Mac is not measured yet; a first useful policy should take tens of minutes to about an hour. If the learned policy doesn't clearly beat the hand-tuned one on `--compiled`, keep mode 0. ## On the robot 1. Copy `core/controller.*` and `core/standup_policy.hpp` into `firmware/esp32/lib/botcore/` and build (`pio run`). 2. Set `standup_mode = 1` on the controller (e.g. in `main.cpp` after creating it). Mode 0 stays one line away. 3. First tests on a soft floor, robot tethered: a learned policy can do things the hand-tuned one never did. Checked here (Linux, Nov 2026): environment passes gymnasium's checker, a 30 k-step smoke training runs end to end, the export matches PyTorch to 1e-7, the controller compiles in the sim and in the ESP32 firmware, and mode 0 (default) behaves exactly as before.

"""Gymnasium environment: learn to take one step DOWN, which the hand-written recipe does 60-75% of. The scripted version is in sim/stairs_descend.py and it works like this: roll at a chosen speed, and a chosen distance before the edge commit to `step_mode` - hold attitude, speed loop off - then hand back once the body has settled. Three numbers, tuned by hand on a grid: roll speed, arming distance, held pitch. It reaches about 65% pooled over risers 60-170 mm. The three numbers are a poor fit for the problem, and that is the opening. A 60 mm lip and a 170 mm step want different speeds and different commitment points, and the robot KNOWS which it faces - the zone array measures the riser to about 13 mm before it ever moves. A fixed recipe cannot use that. A policy can. What the policy controls each 20 ms: a[0] wheel speed command, 0 .. V_MAX a[1] commit: > 0 arms step_mode (latching, one-way - a step is not something to change your mind about halfway down) a[2] the attitude to hold across the lip, STEP_LO .. STEP_HI rad What it sees (9 floats): distance to the edge and the measured riser - both as the array would give them, with noise, not the truth - pitch, pitch rate, wheel speed, whether it has committed, whether the wheels are unloaded, time, and the last speed command. Reward design, with the three mistakes from the nod's reward already paid for: * never stepping has to cost more than a bad step, or refusing is correct arithmetic and the policy learns to stand at the edge for ever. NO_STEP < -(FELL * worst-case rate) is the test. * the landing bonus is SCALED by how gently it lands, never flat. The nod's run-2 policy slammed through a flat catch window at 16.9 rad/s because the bonus did not care. * every term telescopes: the policy is paid the improvement, not the state, so nothing can be farmed by sitting still. """ import math, pathlib, sys import numpy as np import gymnasium as gym HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent ROOT = HERE.parent sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "sim")) from botsim import BotSim, CTRL_DT # noqa: E402 from stairs_probe import model_xml # noqa: E402 EDGE = 1.2 HOLD = 10 # sim ticks per policy step: 20 ms, fast enough to place the commitment T_MAX = 6.0 RISE_LO, RISE_HI = 0.06, 0.17 TREAD_LO, TREAD_HI = 0.24, 0.32 D0_LO, D0_HI = 0.30, 0.55 V_MAX = 0.45 STEP_LO, STEP_HI = -0.12, 0.06 # rad to hold across the lip (negative = heels first) EDGE_SD = 0.013 # m: the zone array knows the edge this well (sim/tof_sensor.py) RISE_SD = 0.013 # m: and the riser about as well LAND_OK = 0.80 # rad: peak pitch above this is a tumble, not a step SETTLE_HOLD = 0.6 # s the settled state must hold before it counts as a step SETTLE_P, SETTLE_V = 0.20, 0.12 # it has to STOP on the tread, not merely be upright while rolling # across it: at 0.35 m/s a policy can "land" and coast straight off # the next edge, and the first version of this reward paid for that SUCCESS = 14.0 # paid only on a landing that is actually a landing, and scaled by it GENTLE = 0.45 # rad: scale of the "how gently" term NO_STEP = -26.0 # never crossing the edge. WORSE than falling, which inverts the nod's # ordering on purpose: for the nod, going over the edge was catastrophic # and declining to look was merely useless, so falling had to cost more. # Here the robot's whole job is to get down, so a robot that stands at the # top for ever has failed completely while a scruffy step is progress. At # -12 it learned exactly that - crossed_rate 0.01 after 800k steps. CROSS = 3.0 # paid ONCE, at the moment the edge is crossed, win or lose FELL = -20.0 PROGRESS_W = 2.0 # telescoping shaping towards the edge STAB_W = 5.0 # telescoping shaping towards "upright and stopped", AFTER the edge only. # Without it every exploratory step ends in a tumble or a run-on and the # two score alike, so there is no gradient towards landing at all: a # random policy crossed 20 times out of 20 and landed none. TIME_COST = 0.02 # The ordering is not enough on its own: what matters is the EXPECTED value of stepping while the # policy is still bad at it. With a crossing bonus paid win or lose, stepping beats refusing once # p(success) > (NO_STEP + FELL + CROSS) / (SUCCESS + CROSS - FELL - CROSS), about 15% here - which a # curriculum of small risers reaches almost immediately. Without it the first run learned, correctly, # never to step at all: crossed_rate sat at 0 for 129k steps. # E[step] = p*(SUCCESS + CROSS) + (1-p)*(FELL + CROSS) must beat NO_STEP _p_break = (NO_STEP - CROSS - FELL) / (SUCCESS - FELL) assert NO_STEP < FELL < 0 and _p_break <= 0.0, ( f"stepping has to be worth trying from the very first episode: with these numbers it needs " f"p(success) > {_p_break:.0%}, and exploration will never get there.") class DescendEnv(gym.Env): metadata = {"render_modes": []} def __init__(self, seed=None, rise=None, tread=None, randomize=True, curriculum=False): self.observation_space = gym.spaces.Box(-5.0, 5.0, (9,), np.float32) self.action_space = gym.spaces.Box(-1.0, 1.0, (3,), np.float32) self.sim = None self.fixed = dict(rise=rise, tread=tread) self.randomize = randomize self.curriculum = curriculum self.rise_hi = 0.07 if curriculum else RISE_HI # ratchets up, see train_descend.py self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) # ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers def set_rise_hi(self, v): """The curriculum: start on lips the robot can already survive, so stepping pays early.""" self.rise_hi = float(v) return self.rise_hi def d_true(self): return EDGE - float(self.sim.d.qpos[0]) def d_est(self): return self.d0_est - (float(self.sim.out.x) - self.x_odom0) def _obs(self): o = self.sim.out return np.array([self.d_est() / 0.5, self.rise_est / 0.17, o.pitch, 0.1 * o.pitch_rate, o.v / V_MAX, 1.0 if self.committed else 0.0, float(o.airborne), self.t / T_MAX, self.a_last], dtype=np.float32) def _run(self, ticks): for _ in range(ticks): o = self.sim.step() if self.crossed: self.peak = max(self.peak, abs(float(o.pitch))) if self.d_true() <= 0 and not self.crossed: self.crossed, self.t_cross = True, self.t self.cross_pay = CROSS if int(o.state) not in (3, 4): # COAST or BALANCE; anything else is a loss return False return True # ------------------------------------------------------------------ gym api def reset(self, seed=None, options=None): if seed is not None: self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) o = options or {} lo, hi = RISE_LO, (o.get("rise_hi") or self.rise_hi) self.rise = o.get("rise") or self.fixed["rise"] or float(self.rng.uniform(lo, hi)) self.tread = o.get("tread") or self.fixed["tread"] or float(self.rng.uniform(TREAD_LO, TREAD_HI)) d0 = o.get("d0") or float(self.rng.uniform(D0_LO, D0_HI)) if self.sim is not None: self.sim.close() sim_seed = int(self.rng.integers(0, 2 ** 31 - 1)) self.sim = BotSim(xml_str=model_xml(self.rise, self.tread, 8, EDGE), seed=sim_seed, randomize=self.randomize) yaw0 = float(self.rng.normal(0, math.radians(1.5))) # it never arrives perfectly square self.sim.place(pitch=0.0, x=EDGE - d0, yaw=yaw0) self.sim.hold(0.6) self.sim.cmd.mode = 0 self.sim.cmd.obstacle_stop = 0 self.sim.cmd.drop_stop = 0 # the fence is exactly what this is learning past self.sim.cmd.step_mode = 0 self.sim.cmd.step_max = 1.6 self.x_odom0 = float(self.sim.out.x) # what the array hands over: an edge and a riser, each with its own error self.d0_est = d0 + float(self.rng.normal(0, EDGE_SD)) self.rise_est = self.rise + float(self.rng.normal(0, RISE_SD)) self.t, self.a_last = 0.0, 0.0 self.committed, self.crossed, self.t_cross = False, False, None self.cross_pay = 0.0 self.best_stab = 0.0 self.settle_t = 0.0 self.peak, self.d_best = 0.0, d0 return self._obs(), {} def step(self, action): a = np.clip(np.asarray(action, dtype=np.float64), -1.0, 1.0) v_cmd = float(0.5 * (a[0] + 1.0) * V_MAX) self.a_last = float(a[0]) if not self.committed and a[1] > 0.0: # one-way: committing is a decision about the next 200 ms, not a knob to wobble self.committed = True self.sim.cmd.step_pitch = float(STEP_LO + 0.5 * (a[2] + 1.0) * (STEP_HI - STEP_LO)) self.sim.cmd.step_mode = 1 self.sim.cmd.v = v_cmd r = -TIME_COST # telescoping progress: paid for getting closer to the edge, once, never for being near it d = max(0.0, self.d_true()) if d < self.d_best: r += PROGRESS_W * (self.d_best - d) / 0.5 self.d_best = d alive = self._run(HOLD) r += self.cross_pay # paid once; the episode cannot farm it self.cross_pay = 0.0 self.t += HOLD * CTRL_DT if self.crossed: o2 = self.sim.out stab = (math.exp(-(abs(float(o2.pitch)) / 0.30) ** 2) * math.exp(-(abs(float(o2.v)) / 0.40) ** 2)) if stab > self.best_stab: # telescoping: paid the improvement, once r += STAB_W * (stab - self.best_stab) self.best_stab = stab if not alive: return self._end(r, fell=True) o = self.sim.out # off the far end of the tread is not a landing, it is the next step taken by accident past = self.d_true() # negative once over the edge if -past > self.tread - 0.04: return self._end(r, ran_on=True) # Settled has to HOLD. Ending the episode the instant the robot is briefly upright and slow # scores a robot that settles and then topples as a clean step, and it put the scripted # baseline at 100% in here against 65-90% in sim/stairs_descend.py - the environment was # easier than the task, which is the one thing a training environment must never be. settled = (self.crossed and self.t - (self.t_cross or 0) > 0.9 and abs(float(o.pitch)) < SETTLE_P and abs(float(o.v)) < SETTLE_V and int(o.state) == 4) self.settle_t = self.settle_t + HOLD * CTRL_DT if settled else 0.0 if self.settle_t >= SETTLE_HOLD: return self._end(r, landed=True) if self.t >= T_MAX: return self._end(r) return self._obs(), r, False, False, self._info() def _info(self, **kw): o = self.sim.out d = dict(success=0.0, fell=0.0, no_step=0.0, ran_on=0.0, crossed=float(self.crossed), peak_deg=math.degrees(self.peak), committed=float(self.committed), rise_mm=1000.0 * self.rise, t_end=self.t, end_pitch_deg=math.degrees(float(o.pitch)), end_v=float(o.v)) d.update(kw) return d def _end(self, r, fell=False, landed=False, ran_on=False): ok = False if fell: r += FELL elif not self.crossed: r += NO_STEP elif landed: # scaled by how gently it went over, never flat: a landing that peaked at 60 degrees is # a tumble the robot happened to survive, and must not pay like a step gentle = math.exp(-(self.peak / GENTLE) ** 2) r += SUCCESS * gentle ok = self.peak < LAND_OK elif ran_on: r += 0.5 * FELL # rolled off the far end of the tread else: r += 0.5 * FELL # crossed, never settled: still on the floor somewhere info = self._info(success=float(ok), fell=float(fell), no_step=float(not self.crossed), ran_on=float(ran_on)) return self._obs(), r, True, False, info def close(self): if self.sim is not None: self.sim.close() self.sim = None

"""Compare the learned stand-up with the hand-tuned one on the same 60 randomised robots as sim/run_tests.py (seeds 3000-3029, face-down and back-down), with the full controller in charge (5 s each, retries allowed). python ml/evaluate.py # the hand-tuned stand-up only python ml/evaluate.py ml/runs/standup/best.zip # + the trained model, run from Python After export_policy.py + rebuilding the library, `--compiled` runs the policy inside the C++ controller (mode 1), which is exactly what the robot will run. """ import sys, math, pathlib import numpy as np from multiprocessing import Pool ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "sim")); sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "ml")) from botsim import BotSim, LIB, CTRL_DT # noqa: E402 def trial(args): # the model path travels in the task, not in a global: multiprocessing uses spawn on # macOS, where a worker re-imports this module and would not see a module-level MODEL. seed, side, mode, model_path = args model = None if mode == "model": from stable_baselines3 import PPO model = PPO.load(model_path, device="cpu") s = BotSim(seed=seed, randomize=True) s.place(pitch=1.8 * side) LIB.bot_standup(s.ctl, {"hand": 0, "model": 2, "compiled": 1}[mode], 0.0) obs = (__import__("ctypes").c_float * 6)() tick = 0 for _ in range(int(5.0 / CTRL_DT)): if model is not None and s.out.state == 2 and tick % 5 == 0: LIB.bot_standup_obs(s.ctl, obs) a, _ = model.predict(np.array(obs, dtype=np.float32), deterministic=True) LIB.bot_standup(s.ctl, 2, float(np.clip(a[0], -1, 1)) * 4.6) tick = tick + 1 if s.out.state == 2 else 0 s.step() L = np.array(s.log); s.close() st = L[:, 1].astype(int) ok = st[-1] == 4 and np.abs(L[-500:, 2]).max() < math.radians(12) up = np.where(st == 4)[0] return ok, (L[up[0], 0] if len(up) else np.nan), float(np.hypot(L[-1, 9] - L[0, 9], L[-1, 10] - L[0, 10])) def run(mode, model_path=None): with Pool() as p: R = p.map(trial, [(3000 + i, side, mode, model_path) for i in range(30) for side in (1, -1)]) ok = [r[0] for r in R] print(f"{mode:9s} face-down {sum(ok[0::2])}/30 back-down {sum(ok[1::2])}/30 " f"median time to upright {np.nanmedian([r[1] for r in R]):.2f} s median travel {np.median([r[2] for r in R]):.2f} m") if __name__ == "__main__": run("hand") if "--compiled" in sys.argv: run("compiled") args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")] if args: run("model", args[0])

""" import argparse, pathlib, sys import numpy as np sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).parent)) from descend_env import DescendEnv, V_MAX, STEP_LO, STEP_HI # noqa: E402 from warmstart_descend import recipe # noqa: E402 RUN = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "runs" / "descend" class Learned: def __init__(self, path): from stable_baselines3 import PPO self.m = PPO.load(path, device="cpu") def reset(self): pass def act(self, obs): return self.m.predict(np.asarray(obs, dtype=np.float32), deterministic=True)[0] class Scripted: def reset(self): self.st = {} def act(self, obs): return recipe(obs, self.st) def score(pol, trials=60, seed0=40_000, rise=None): env = DescendEnv(seed=seed0) rows = [] for k in range(trials): obs, _ = env.reset(seed=seed0 + k, options=dict(rise=rise) if rise else None) pol.reset() while True: obs, r, done, _, info = env.step(pol.act(obs)) if done: break rows.append(info) env.close() m = lambda k: float(np.mean([x[k] for x in rows])) peaks = [x["peak_deg"] for x in rows if x["crossed"]] return dict(success=m("success"), crossed=m("crossed"), fell=m("fell"), ran_on=m("ran_on"), no_step=m("no_step"), peak=float(np.mean(peaks)) if peaks else float("nan"), n=trials) def line(tag, s): print(f" {tag:<34} ok={s['success']:5.2f} stepped={s['crossed']:5.2f} fell={s['fell']:5.2f} " f"ran on={s['ran_on']:5.2f} never={s['no_step']:5.2f} peak={s['peak']:5.1f} deg") def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("model", nargs="?", default=None) ap.add_argument("--trials", type=int, default=60) ap.add_argument("--all", action="store_true") ap.add_argument("--sweep", action="store_true") a = ap.parse_args() print(f"\n\033[1mheld-out staircases (seeds 40000+), {a.trials} each\033[0m") if a.all: cands = sorted(RUN.glob("ckpt/*.zip"), key=lambda p: int(p.stem.split("_")[1])) + \ [p for p in (RUN / "latest.zip", RUN / "bc.zip") if p.exists()] best = (None, -1) line("scripted recipe", score(Scripted(), a.trials)) for c in cands: s = score(Learned(c), a.trials) line(c.name, s) if s["success"] > best[1]: best = (c, s["success"]) print(f"\n winner: {best[0].name if best[0] else '--'} at {best[1]:.2f}") return pol = Learned(a.model) if a.model else Scripted() line(pathlib.Path(a.model).name if a.model else "scripted recipe", score(pol, a.trials)) if a.sweep: for rise in (0.06, 0.08, 0.10, 0.13, 0.15, 0.17): line(f" riser {rise*1000:.0f} mm", score(pol, max(20, a.trials // 3), rise=rise)) if __name__ == "__main__": main()

"""Score a nod-timing policy, or the scripted baseline, on held-out staircases. python ml/evaluate_stairs.py # the scripted baseline python ml/evaluate_stairs.py ml/runs/stairs/latest.zip # a trained policy python ml/evaluate_stairs.py ml/runs/stairs/latest.zip --sweep # per-riser breakdown The gate is this script, not the eval reward in TensorBoard: the per-episode reward is nearly bimodal (the riser comes out or it does not), which is exactly the kind of signal that made `best.zip` useless for the stand-up. Seeds 20000+ are never used in training. A success means all three at once: the riser measured to within 20 mm, the robot still upright, and at least 100 mm of landing left between the wheels and the drop at the worst moment of the episode. """ import argparse, math, pathlib, sys import numpy as np sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).parent)) from stairs_env import StairsLookEnv, RISE_LO, RISE_HI # noqa: E402 from stairs_baseline import Scripted, score # noqa: E402 class Learned: """The trained policy, acting deterministically (the mean action), exactly as the robot would.""" def __init__(self, path): from stable_baselines3 import PPO self.model = PPO.load(path, device="cpu") def reset(self): pass def act(self, obs): return self.model.predict(np.asarray(obs, dtype=np.float32), deterministic=True)[0] def line(tag, s): print(f" {tag:<22} {s['success']:5.2f} {s['measured']:5.2f} {s['err']:6.0f} +-{s['err_sd']:4.0f} mm " f"{s['d_peak']:6.0f} mm {s['margin']:6.0f} mm {s['margin_min']:6.0f} mm {s['fell']:5.2f} {s['off']:5.2f}") def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("model", nargs="?", default=None) ap.add_argument("--trials", type=int, default=30) ap.add_argument("--sweep", action="store_true", help="break the result down by riser height") ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20_000) a = ap.parse_args() env = StairsLookEnv() pol = Learned(a.model) if a.model else Scripted() tag = pathlib.Path(a.model).name if a.model else "scripted baseline" print(f"\n\033[1m{tag}: {a.trials} held-out episodes (seeds {a.seed}+)\033[0m") print(f" {'':<22} {'ok':>5} {'meas':>5} {'riser error':>13} {'d at peak':>9} " f"{'margin':>9} {'worst':>9} {'fell':>5} {'off':>5}") line("randomised stairs", score(env, pol, a.trials, seed0=a.seed)) if a.sweep: for rise in (0.08, 0.10, 0.13, 0.15, 0.17): line(f"riser {rise*1000:.0f} mm", score(env, pol, max(10, a.trials // 2), seed0=a.seed + 1000, rise=rise, tread=0.30)) env.close() if __name__ == "__main__": main()

"""Export a trained PPO policy to core/standup_policy.hpp (plain C++ arrays, no ML library on the robot). python ml/export_policy.py ml/runs/standup/best.zip The policy is the actor's mean (deterministic): tanh MLP 6 -> 64 -> 64 -> 1, output clamped to [-1, 1]. ~4.6 k multiply-adds every 10 ms: well under 0.1 ms on the ESP32-S3. Then rebuild (simulator: core/build_lib.sh; robot: pio run) and check with `python ml/evaluate.py --compiled`. ml/run_training.sh does all of this in the right order. """ import sys, pathlib import numpy as np import torch from stable_baselines3 import PPO ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] OUT = ROOT / "core" / "standup_policy.hpp" def arr(name, a): flat = ", ".join(f"{v:.8g}f" for v in a.reshape(-1)) return f"inline constexpr float {name}[{a.size}] = {{{flat}}};\n" def main(path): model = PPO.load(path, device="cpu") pol = model.policy lin = [m for m in pol.mlp_extractor.policy_net if isinstance(m, torch.nn.Linear)] + [pol.action_net] acts = [m for m in pol.mlp_extractor.policy_net if not isinstance(m, torch.nn.Linear)] assert all(isinstance(m, torch.nn.Tanh) for m in acts), "export expects tanh hidden layers" W = [l.weight.detach().numpy().astype(np.float32) for l in lin] B = [l.bias.detach().numpy().astype(np.float32) for l in lin] sizes = [W[0].shape[1]] + [w.shape[0] for w in W] assert sizes[0] == 6 and sizes[-1] == 1, sizes src = [f"// Learned stand-up policy. GENERATED by ml/export_policy.py from {pathlib.Path(path).name}: do not edit by hand.\n", "#pragma once\n#include <cmath>\n\n", "constexpr int STANDUP_NOBS = 6; // inputs: see Controller::standup_obs()\n", "constexpr int STANDUP_HOLD = 5; // the policy acts every 5 control ticks (10 ms)\n", "constexpr float STANDUP_TIMEOUT = 2.0f; // s from the start of the push\n", "constexpr bool STANDUP_POLICY_TRAINED = true;\n\nnamespace standup_nn {\n"] for i, (w, b) in enumerate(zip(W, B)): src += [arr(f"W{i}", w), arr(f"B{i}", b)] src.append("} // namespace standup_nn\n\n") src.append("// returns the push for both motors together as a fraction of 2 x torque_limit, in [-1, 1]\n") src.append("inline float standup_policy(const float* o) {\n using namespace standup_nn;\n") src.append(f" float h0[{sizes[1]}], h1[{sizes[2]}];\n") src.append(f" for (int j = 0; j < {sizes[1]}; ++j) {{ float s = B0[j]; for (int i = 0; i < {sizes[0]}; ++i) s += W0[j * {sizes[0]} + i] * o[i]; h0[j] = std::tanh(s); }}\n") src.append(f" for (int j = 0; j < {sizes[2]}; ++j) {{ float s = B1[j]; for (int i = 0; i < {sizes[1]}; ++i) s += W1[j * {sizes[1]} + i] * h0[i]; h1[j] = std::tanh(s); }}\n") src.append(f" float y = B2[0]; for (int i = 0; i < {sizes[2]}; ++i) y += W2[i] * h1[i];\n") src.append(" return y > 1.f ? 1.f : (y < -1.f ? -1.f : y);\n}\n") OUT.write_text("".join(src)) # self-check against PyTorch on random inputs x = np.random.default_rng(0).uniform(-2, 2, (100, 6)).astype(np.float32) ref = np.clip(model.policy.get_distribution(torch.tensor(x)).distribution.mean.detach().numpy()[:, 0], -1, 1) h = np.tanh(x @ W[0].T + B[0]); h = np.tanh(h @ W[1].T + B[1]); y = np.clip((h @ W[2].T + B[2])[:, 0], -1, 1) print(f"wrote {OUT} ({OUT.stat().st_size // 1024} kB), max |numpy - torch| = {np.abs(y - ref).max():.2e}") if __name__ == "__main__": main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else str(pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "runs" / "standup" / "best.zip"))
